## Session 177 (2026-07-28) — offline log analysis narrowed the stall's own "stalled" field to a wall-clock artifact (not the real threshold) and found a candidate shared internal ceiling instead; landed and soaked a targeted `waitForPostSwapAck` producer-side instrument; this run's soak did not reproduce the stall, recurring instead to the s84 `frameStartReset` SIGBUS (2nd occurrence, softening its "fluke" label) with the new instrument showing a clean negative control

### What ran

Per NEXT.md's step 1 (offline log re-analysis, no rebuild): dispatched a background agent to grep the two s176 stall logs (`scenenodedepthguard1`/`2`) for the field values at each run's last real `[vi-fs-decision]` transition before the stall became permanent, looking for a shared threshold.

In parallel, source-read the RT64-side decision logic (`lib/rt64/src/hle/rt64_state.cpp` ~2828-2934) and the guest-side per-frame producer chain (`runHangarSelectionFrame` -> `waitForPrevFrameDone` -> `waitForPostSwapAck`, `funcs_40.c`/`funcs_3.c`/`funcs_5.c`) before writing any new instrument, per rule 6.

### Result 1: the "stalled" field is wall-clock-defined, not a hidden counter threshold — NEXT.md's framing needed correcting before instrumenting further

Source read of `rt64_state.cpp:2841-2843` shows `stalled` is computed directly from `std::chrono::steady_clock` — `(now - g_rs64LastAdvance) > 100.0ms` — not from any guest tick or resource count. NEXT.md's s176 framing ("most plausibly tick-count or resource-count based") was an unverified guess; it's refuted at the source level. The real open question was never "what value does `stalled` cross" (it's just elapsed wall time) — it's "why does the pending workload's `fbPairCount` (the `pairs` field) stay 0 indefinitely once stalled," i.e. why the guest stops registering new framebuffer pairs at all.

### Result 2 (background agent, offline grep, both prior runs' existing logs — no rebuild): a candidate shared internal ceiling, not a wall-clock/tick threshold

At each run's last `stalled=0` line: `rdpFs`/`skSeen`/`skNoTrig` cluster in a narrow band (~3175-3802) in **both** runs despite run 1 running 87% longer in wall-clock time before its onset (141.8s vs 75.8s) than run 2. If these counters were wall-clock- or tick-scaled, they should differ by roughly that same 87% — instead they're within 5-8% of each other. (`skPair0` is the one field that actually is wall-clock-scaled, ~50x apart, and should be discounted as a threshold candidate.) This is a single-source (one background-agent pass over 2 runs) but well-reasoned candidate: some fixed-size resource (buffer/queue-slot/semaphore count in the ~3500-3800 range) may be exhausted at roughly the same *operation count* regardless of which scene the process is in, rather than the stall being purely wall-clock/tick-gated. Not yet confirmed by a 3rd data point.

### Result 3: landed and soaked a targeted producer-side instrument (`ROGUESQ_LOG_SWAP_ACK_WAIT`) — this soak did not reproduce the stall, so it did not test the hypothesis end-to-end, but it did produce a clean negative control on the instrument itself

Source trace: `runHangarSelectionFrame` (`static_5_800AAD9C`, `funcs_40.c:5464`) calls `waitForPrevFrameDone` (`funcs_3.c:8231`) as the very first thing in its per-frame body, before any animation/camera/`submitGfxFrame` work; `waitForPrevFrameDone` calls `waitForPostSwapAck` (`funcs_5.c:6013`), which — only when two guest flags (0x8011A8C9 and 0x8011A8C8) are both set — loops on `osRecvMesg_recomp` waiting for a swap-ack message before returning. This is the only point in the per-frame producer where it can block before producing new framebuffer pairs, making it the natural target for "does the producer stop being invoked, or does it get stuck once invoked" (NEXT.md's own step-2 framing).

Landed `fixup_game_funcs.py` patches (funcs_5.c): entry counter + pre-recv/post-recv logging around the `osRecvMesg_recomp` call, gated `ROGUESQ_LOG_SWAP_ACK_WAIT`. Regenerated via `N64Recomp` -> `fixup_game_funcs.py` (applied exactly once, confirmed via grep on the fixup log: `funcs_5.c: waitForPostSwapAck entry diagnostic patched x1` / `... pre/post-recv diagnostic patched x1`) -> `cmake --build` (exit 0, only pre-existing SDL2-version linker warnings).

One soak (`swapackwait1`, same env block as `scenenodedepthguard2` plus the new flag): the graphics-task-submission stall **did not recur this run** — instead the process crashed (`CRASH: 2`, one `[CRASH]` block) to **a recurrence of the s84 `frameStartReset` SIGBUS** (backtrace: `frameStartReset` (x2, see below) <- `static_5_800C9BF0` <- `menuOverlayInit` <- `mainGameLoop`), at wall ~146.5s, origin `0x006A2900` width 640 (the same post-leave cutscene window s162/s176-run-1 identified) — i.e. this run got further than either s176 stall run (`rdpFs` reached 4125 vs. 3563-3746 at the other runs' stall onsets) before dying to an unrelated bug first. The backtrace shows `frameStartReset + 532` twice in a row; source-checked (`funcs_3.c:7969` onward) confirms **zero self-calls** in the function body, so this is very likely the same kind of stack-unwind duplication artifact already established for `advancePlayerAnimationPhase` in s87/88, not true recursion.

The new instrument itself behaved exactly as designed and gives a genuine (if narrow) negative control: 7391 `enter` events, 10033 `pre-recv`/10033 `post-recv` (perfectly matched — every single blocking wait this run completed and returned; the higher pre/post-recv count vs. enter count is expected, since the function's own loop can iterate more than once per call when the second flag stays set). The last 3 calls before the crash (`call=7388/7389/7390`) all show clean enter/pre-recv/post-recv triples, with the crash landing immediately after `call=7390 post-recv` — i.e. `waitForPostSwapAck` was not blocked and was not in-flight at the moment of the crash. **This is a negative control on "the producer is parked in this specific wait" for THIS run's failure mode only** — it says nothing about the original graphics-task-submission stall, since that stall did not occur this run to be tested against.

### Rules out / narrows

- Refutes NEXT.md's literal "tick-count or resource-count threshold explains the `stalled` field" framing — `stalled` is wall-clock by construction, confirmed at the source, not a threshold of any kind.
- Does not refute (nor confirm) the underlying `waitForPostSwapAck`-blocks-forever hypothesis for the graphics-task-submission stall specifically — no data point yet, since this soak crashed via a different, already-catalogued bug before ever reaching a stalled state.
- Weakens s85's "frameStartReset was a fluke" framing: that call was made after only 2 non-recurrences following the single s84 occurrence; this session adds a 2nd real occurrence (3rd total data point, now 2/3 sessions where the crash-family gauntlet reached this same site), suggesting it is at least occasionally recurring rather than a one-off, though still far rarer than the family's most-recurring classes.

### Landed (this session)

- `N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`: `waitForPostSwapAck` entry + pre/post-recv diagnostic (`ROGUESQ_LOG_SWAP_ACK_WAIT`), `N64Recomp` sibling checkout (uncommitted, same posture as flagged since s90 — see Housekeeping).
- `scratch/agent/run_swapackwait1.sh` (copy of `run_scenenodedepthguard2.sh`, tag renamed, one flag added) — gitignored, not tracked.
- This repo's tracked files: `scratch/agent/NEXT.md`, `docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md`, this entry.

### Next

1. **Re-run the same `swapackwait1` recipe** (or extend `STICK_SCHEDULE` to try to reach a 3rd data point) specifically to catch the instrument DURING an actual graphics-task-submission stall — this session's soak crashed via an unrelated bug before ever reaching that state, so the instrument is armed and validated but still untested against its actual target. Watch for: last log line is `pre-recv` with no matching `post-recv` and no further `enter` ever (confirms blocked-forever-in-`osRecvMesg`), vs. `enter`/`pre-recv`/`post-recv` continuing to cycle normally throughout the stall window (refutes this mechanism, points back at the RT64-side gate logic per NEXT.md's original outcome-2 branch).
2. If the shared-ceiling candidate (Result 2, ~3500-3800 on `rdpFs`/`skSeen`/`skNoTrig`) survives a 3rd occurrence at a similar value, that becomes the priority lead over the producer-side instrument — it would give a concrete reproduction target (drive the counter to ~3500-3800) instead of waiting on wall-clock.
3. `tickSongSequence`'s 2 unguarded list walks (funcs_25.c:5018-5046, 5050-5077, found s174, not guarded) — still open, still lower priority.
4. `submitSceneNodeRender+16780` (s171) — still open, still lowest priority of the characterized-but-unfixed leads.

## Session 178 (2026-07-28) — first-ever crash-free capture of the actual graphics-task-submission stall with the producer instrument armed: refutes BOTH of s177's anticipated outcomes, finds instead that the per-frame producer chain (and graphics-task submission itself) simply stop being invoked, closely correlated in log position; independently confirms the s176/177 "shared ceiling" candidate with a 3rd data point landing in the predicted band

### What ran

Per NEXT.md step 1: copied `run_swapackwait1.sh` to `run_swapackwait2.sh` (tag rename only, same env block/instruments/`STICK_SCHEDULE`) and ran one soak. No code changes this session — pure re-run + offline analysis of the resulting ~3.6 GB / 73.5M-line `run.log`, all via targeted `grep`/`awk` passes (never `cat`/`Read` on the file itself), per the "capture once, analyze many" rule.

### Result 1: process survived the entire 120s hold + grace window alive, no crash — the first clean capture of the stall itself under this instrument

Driver summary: `CRASH: 0`, `game process still alive; killing` (script had to SIGKILL it after the hold+grace window elapsed, vs. every prior `swapackwait*`/`scenenodedepthguard*` soak either crashing or the process exiting on its own). `fs max: 3579`, last `[vi] update_screen` line at guest-time-equivalent counter #16064, `origin=0x00696100 width=640`. This is the actual graphics-task-submission stall (`[vi-fs-decision] stalled=1 pairs=0` persisting), not a crash — the first time this exact soak recipe has reproduced it since the instrument was landed (s177's one prior attempt crashed on `frameStartReset` before ever reaching a stalled state).

### Result 2: 3rd data point CONFIRMS the s176/177 "shared ceiling" candidate — promote from single-source candidate to a real, narrow, reproducible band

The persistent stall's `rdpFs` plateaus at exactly **3579** (`skSeen=3604`, `skNoTrig=3466`), and the transition from `stalled=0` to a *persistent* `stalled=1` happens at counter `#14080` with `rdpFs=3560` already — both values squarely inside the `~3175-3802` band s177 found (single-source, background-agent grep) across the two s176 runs. Three independent occurrences (s176 run 1: onset ~3746; s176 run 2: onset ~3563; this run: onset ~3560, plateau 3579) now cluster inside a band roughly 200-250 wide out of a run that otherwise varies wildly in wall-clock/tick terms — this is now **two-source-equivalent** (s177's background-agent grep + this session's direct verification) and should be treated as an established, reproducible pattern: some fixed-size resource (buffer/queue-slot/semaphore count around 3500-3800) is exhausted at roughly the same *operation count* across runs, not gated by wall-clock or scene state. Not yet root-caused to a specific counter/buffer, but now a concrete, driveable target (any soak whose `rdpFs` approaches ~3500-3600 should be watched closely for the stall).

Nuance: within this run, `[vi-fs-decision]` also logged one single, isolated `stalled=0 reason=no-trigger` sample at `#15296` in the middle of an otherwise-continuous `stalled=1` run (#14080 through #16064 at kill time) — a one-tick blip, not a real recovery (no framebuffer pair was ever registered around it, `pairs=0` throughout). Not investigated further; noted so a future session doesn't mistake it for evidence of intermittent recovery.

### Result 3: the swap-ack-wait instrument refutes BOTH of NEXT.md's anticipated outcomes — a 3rd, more specific mechanism instead

Neither of s177's two hypothesized outcomes happened:
- **Not** "blocked forever inside `osRecvMesg_recomp`" — every `[swap-ack-wait]` call this run completed cleanly: 5768 `enter` events, 9447 `pre-recv`, 9447 `post-recv` (perfectly matched, zero orphans), and the very last call (`call=5767`) shows a complete `enter`/`pre-recv`/`post-recv` triple with nothing dangling.
- **Not** "keeps cycling normally throughout the stall window" either — `[swap-ack-wait]` simply **stops appearing in the log at all** after `call=5767` (line ~64,036,414), for the remaining ~9.5M lines of the run (log ends at line 73,542,139) until the process was killed. The per-frame producer chain (`runHangarSelectionFrame` -> `waitForPrevFrameDone` -> `waitForPostSwapAck`) was never invoked again, not stuck mid-call.

This closely correlates with graphics task submission itself: the last `[lle task]` entry (RSP graphics-task submission — literally what "graphics-task-submission stall" names) is at line 64,761,412, and the driver summary's `lle tasks: 5767` count matches `[swap-ack-wait]`'s last call number almost exactly. Both stop within ~700K log lines of each other, both far short of the log's end — i.e. **graphics-task submission genuinely halts** (not merely "this one wait call never returns"), and it halts at essentially the same point the calling per-frame loop stops iterating.

The process is not a full hang, though: `[rs-malloc]` continues logging until line 67,300,546 (further than graphics/swap-ack-wait but still short of the end), and `[rs-free-walk]` dominates the log's final ~2 MB, still firing at the moment of the kill — a **staggered subsystem shutdown**, not a simultaneous freeze. Matches the pre-existing CURRENT-TRUTH characterization ("process alive... heap allocation keep running to the end of the log") only partially: heap *free-walking* runs to the very end this session, but heap *allocation* (`rs-malloc`) and graphics-task submission both stop well before the end, a nuance not previously documented.

`UnhandledJump: 873` this run — checked directly (not assumed): 867/873 matched lines decode as `Unhandled jump target 0x0231|0x17F0 in microcode factor5_ucode`, the already-documented benign RSP-microcode-fallback pattern, not a guest-CPU regression (the remaining ~6 are truncated duplicates of the same two lines at a log-rotation boundary, not new patterns).

### Rules out / narrows

- **Refutes** "the producer is blocked forever inside `osRecvMesg_recomp`" (s177's outcome-1 hypothesis) — clean, fully-matched enter/pre-recv/post-recv counts through the last call, no orphaned wait.
- **Refutes** "the producer keeps cycling normally throughout the stall" (s177's outcome-2 hypothesis, would have pointed at the RT64-side gate logic alone) — the producer stops being invoked at all, well before the stall's own tail end.
- **Reframes the root-cause direction**: the bug is not inside `waitForPostSwapAck`/`osRecvMesg_recomp` itself — it's upstream, in whatever schedules/loops `runHangarSelectionFrame` (its caller, or the guest OS thread executing it). That loop or thread stops iterating/being resumed at almost exactly the point graphics-task submission stops, which is a new, more specific, and more answerable question than "does this one wait call return."
- **Promotes** the s176/177 shared-ceiling candidate (`rdpFs`/`skSeen`/`skNoTrig` ~3175-3802) from single-source to a 3-occurrence-confirmed pattern.
- Partially corrects the pre-existing CURRENT-TRUTH stall characterization: heap *allocation* and graphics-task submission both stop before the log's end this run, only heap *free-walking* runs to the very end — "audio ucode and heap allocation keep running to the end of the log" (s162 wording) does not hold uniformly across all subsystems in this occurrence.

## Session 180 (2026-07-28) — 3rd `schedcaller` attempt reproduced the sustained graphics-task-submission stall crash-free for the first time, and found a source-confirmed, tightly-timed root-cause mechanism: the s84 UAF guard silently drops the scheduler's "next thread" turn instead of retrying or waking its caller

Per rule 8 this was the 3rd (and last allowed) attempt at the `schedcaller`-shape soak (s177 1st miss, s179 2nd miss, both to `frameStartReset`). Copied `run_schedcaller1.sh` verbatim to `run_schedcaller2.sh` (only the tag string changed) and reran.

**Outcome: full success on both axes.** Driver summary: `CRASH: 0`, `hold done wall=137s`, `done wall=161s`, process still alive at the end (driver killed it) — the **first fully crash-free soak to ever reach the target stall state**, previously the two outcomes had been mutually exclusive (s88's one crash-free run never reached the ~90-115s post-leave window this stall lives in; every run that reached it before now died to something else first). `fs max: 3747`, inside the s176-179 `~3175-3802` candidate-ceiling band (5th data point).

**The stall is genuinely sustained, not a blip.** `stalled=1 pairs=0` fired 301 times total; the tail of the run (`[vi-fs-decision]` decisions **#8000 through #16256**, the last line in the log) is one unbroken run of `stalled=1 pairs=0` with `rdpFs` frozen at exactly 3747 throughout — over 8000 consecutive stalled decisions, not isolated blips like s179's 43. `[lle task]`/`[runner] task` submission stopped for good at task `#4780`.

**Discriminating result for NEXT.md's own question.** `[hangar-loop]`'s last firing is `n=538` at run.log line 3489078; the very next lines are `[swap-ack-wait] call=4781 enter/pre-recv/post-recv` (lines 3489079-3489082) — a clean, fully-matched call, no orphan. Neither instrument fires even once more anywhere in the remaining ~400k lines of log (confirmed by full-file `grep -c`: 539 total `[hangar-loop]` lines, 19764 total `[swap-ack-wait]` lines, both accounted for by their last-seen line numbers). This is NEXT.md's first bullet outcome exactly: **the outer polling loop itself stops iterating** (it does not keep running while its callee silently skips the wait) — pointing at the guest OS thread executing it (thread id 3, confirmed again this run — 2nd confirmation that one consistent thread owns this loop) simply never being resumed/scheduled again.

**Root mechanism found, source-confirmed, single-run positive control.** Between `[swap-ack-wait] call=4781 post-recv` and the stall's onset, exactly one `[thr-resume-skip]` line fires in the entire run (`ROGUESQ_LOG_THREAD_RESUME` was 0 all run per s93's confound finding, so this is the always-on cheap-atomic path, not the verbose log):
```
[runner] task #4780 exit=1 dl_ptr=0x80751908 tris=578 texrects=0 fillrects=0 syncs=0 cimg=2 depth=2
[thr-resume-skip] tag=run_next id=0 ctx=0x0 live=0 bad_total=1
[vi-fs-decision] #7967 FIRE reason=stalled ...
[vi-fs-decision] #7968 SKIP reason=no-trigger ... stalled=0
[vi] update_screen #8000 ...
[vi-fs-decision] #8000 SKIP reason=pair=0 ... stalled=1 pairs=0   <- sustained from here to EOF
```
This is only the 2nd positive control the s84 gate has ever gotten (1st was s88, `bad_total=1`, process survived unaffected) — but this time it's tightly correlated with the stall onset rather than incidental. Read the gate's own source (`lib/N64ModernRuntime/ultramodern/src/threads.cpp:198-258`, `resume_thread_tagged`) to understand the mechanism rather than guessing from the log line alone:
- `run_next_thread` (line 264-272) pops the front of `running_queue` and calls `resume_thread_tagged(to_run, "run_next")`.
- If `to_run`'s context is `bad` (null, or not in the live-context set — the exact s83/s70-72 UAF signature), `resume_thread_tagged` prints `[thr-resume-skip]` and **returns without signalling anything** (line 216-220) — it does **not** retry with the next queue entry, and does **not** wake whichever thread called into the scheduler expecting a handoff.
- `run_next_thread_and_wait` (line 274-278, called from `osStopThread` and — critically — `mesgqueue.cpp`'s `do_recv`/`do_send` blocking paths at lines 105/143, which is what the guest `osRecvMesg`/`osSendMesg` blocking loop compiles down to) works by popping the next thread, then **waiting on its own context to be resumed** (`wait_for_resumed(cur_context)`). Nothing else in this call chain will ever signal that context if the popped thread was silently dropped by the guard above.

**This fully explains the observed stall mechanically, not just correlatively:** thread 3 (the hangar-loop thread) reaches `waitForPostSwapAck`'s underlying `osRecvMesg`, finds the swap-ack queue empty, inserts itself into `blocked_on_recv`, and calls `run_next_thread_and_wait` to yield — which pops thread **id 0** off the running queue to hand off execution. Thread 0's context is bad (already UAF'd/torn-down, same corruption family as s70-s94), so the s84 guard correctly refuses to signal it (avoiding the SIGBUS this run — hence `CRASH: 0`) but returns having done nothing else. Thread 3's own context is never signalled back, so it blocks forever in `wait_for_resumed`. If thread 0 was also the thread that would eventually have serviced the swap-ack message queue (i.e. would have called `do_send` on it), the deadlock is permanent and total: nobody is left to either wake thread 3 directly or produce the message it's waiting on. **This reframes the multi-session "graphics-task-submission stall" as very likely a direct, known side effect of the s84 crash-avoidance gate**: the gate trades a SIGBUS crash for a silent, permanent scheduler stall by dropping the "next" thread's turn instead of recovering from it. Not yet a 2nd independent confirmation (rule 4) — this is one run, one firing — but the timing (`[thr-resume-skip]` immediately followed by the stall's onset, with zero other candidate events in between) and the source-level mechanism (a proven silent-drop-with-no-retry, not a hand-wavy correlation) make this the strongest lead this investigation has produced since it began at s176.

**Not yet established, flagged for next session:** what guest thread **id 0** actually is (name/role/priority) — needs a source read of thread-creation call sites (`osCreateThread` call sites with their `id`/`pri` arguments), not a rebuild. Likely candidate given the message-queue mechanism above: whichever thread is expected to send the per-frame swap-ack message that `waitForPostSwapAck` waits on. Confirming this would be the natural 2nd independent line of evidence before this enters the "current truth" summary as more than a strong single-run lead.

**Stability/control summary this run:** `missing-func: 0`, `UnhandledJump: 0`, `ost-wb SKIP_OOB: 10` (routine), `thr-resume bad=1: 0` (this reports only the verbose-log path's own counter, which was off — the always-on cheap-atomic path is what actually fired, see above; do not read this field as contradicting the finding). No other crash-guard family fired; no `[CRASH]` block at all this run.

**Full detail**: this entry. No code changes this session (pure soak + source read, no rebuild). Soak artifacts: `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/schedcaller2/` (run.log 179 MB, screenshots), driver summary `scratch/agent/schedcaller2_driver.log`, driver script `scratch/agent/run_schedcaller2.sh`, extracted stall-onset lines `scratch/agent/s180_stalled_lines.txt`.

## Session 181 (2026-07-28) — refuted s180's "id 0 = single specific thread" premise; landed and validated an always-on thread-identity instrument; one soak, died early to a new-looking crash before reaching the stall

Followed NEXT.md's step 1 exactly: source-read only, no rebuild, before designing any fix. Grepped every `osCreateThread_recomp(` call site in `N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/*.c` (11 hits, one is the `funcs.h` declaration) and read each one's argument setup back to where `$a1` (the `id` argument, `ctx->r5`) is assigned.

**Finding: `id` is not a unique per-thread identifier in this game — id=0 is the default/shared id used by most non-worker threads.** Of 10 real call sites, 8 pass a literal `id=0` (`ADD32(0,0)` into `ctx->r5`) and only 2 pass a dynamically-loaded id (one loads from a caller-supplied struct field, generic thread-spawn helper). The 8 literal-id=0 sites, decoded from their neighboring `entry`/`pri` argument setup, are: `idle_thread_handle` (entry `0x800017A0`, pri 10) spawning `thread3_video_handle` (entry `0x80001088`, pri 9), which itself spawns a child at entry `0x800016AC` (pri 127); a boot function creating 3 more threads back-to-back (entries `0x80019868`/`0x80019BF4`/`0x8001C328`, pri 117/122/122); one more standalone creator (entry `0x80002E10`, pri 118). This directly contradicts NEXT.md's framing ("identify what guest thread id 0 is" as if it names one thread) — **refuted**, not just unconfirmed.

**Confirmed by runtime data, not just static source-reading.** `osCreateThread`'s real implementation (`lib/N64ModernRuntime/ultramodern/src/threads.cpp:355`, `t->id = id`) proves the guest `id` argument is exactly the field the `[thr-resume-skip]`/`[thr-resume]` logs print — no host-side remapping. Landed a new always-on, unconditional log line at thread-creation time (`[thr-create-id] id=%d thr=%p pri=%d entry=0x%08X thr_rdram=0x%08X`, right after `t->context = context;` in `osCreateThread`, `threads.cpp`) plus two new fields (`thr=%p pri=%d`) on the existing cheap `[thr-resume-skip]` line — both changes are pure `lib/` host C++, no guest-code regen needed. Rebuilt clean (`cmake --build`, warnings only pre-existing SDL2-version-mismatch linker warnings). Exported patches (`submodule-patches/export.sh`) — committed this session per the hard rule.

One soak (`schedguard1`, copy of `run_schedcaller2.sh` verbatim except the tag) confirms the instrument works and extends the finding with real runtime addresses:

Positive control: 18/18 fired, matching exactly the source-read prediction (8 literal-id=0 boot/idle/video/audio threads, plus the already-known id=1 PI-DMA-worker and id=3 mainBootstrapWorker from s93). **At least 9 distinct threads share id=0** in a normal run — idle, video, an unnamed video-child, 3 boot-sequence threads, one more unnamed one, and (via the `thr_rdram` address match to s70/71) the **audio playback thread `runAiAudioStreamPlaybackLoop`**. A bare `[thr-resume-skip] id=0` therefore cannot, by itself, tell you which of these was dropped — `thr=%p` now can, by cross-referencing this same run's `[thr-create-id]` lines for the matching host pointer.

**Rules out:** "id 0 in the skip log identifies a specific known thread (e.g. the swap-ack producer)" as a safe assumption for any future fix design — a fix keyed on `id==0` alone would be as likely to be dropping the idle thread, the video thread, the audio thread, or any of 3 anonymous boot threads as it would the actual swap-ack-relevant one. ## Session 182 (2026-07-28) — found and fixed a real gap in the s78 refuse gate: it stops FB-map pollution but not a downstream unbounded RDRAM read, root-causing a new crash class; validated fix reached one attempt further into the hold window before an unrelated, already-catalogued Metal-internal SIGSEGV

Per NEXT.md's step 1, re-ran the `schedcaller`-shape soak (`schedguard2`, copy of s181's `run_schedguard1.sh` verbatim except the tag) to try to reach the sustained graphics-task-submission stall with the `[thr-create-id]`/`thr=%p` instrument armed.

**`schedguard2` did not reach the stall — died even earlier than s181's `schedguard1`** (hold-iter 1, ~1s into the 120s hold, vs. s181's ~7s) to a brand-new crash: SIGBUS (signal 10) inside `RT64::FramebufferStorage::store`'s `memcpy` (`rt64_framebuffer_storage.cpp:30`), called from `RT64::State::fullSync`'s color/depth-read-into-storage lambda (`rt64_state.cpp:2227`/`2271`). `[thr-resume-skip]` fired 0 times — 0 new data toward s180's still-open 2nd-confirmation requirement.

**Source-read the crash before instrumenting further (per rule 5).** `FramebufferStorage::store` does an unchecked `memcpy(rdramData.data() + dstIndex, data, size)` where `data = &RDRAM[storageAddress]` — the caller computes `storageAddress`/`readFbBytes` from a `Framebuffer`'s own `width`/`height`/`address` fields with **no bounds check against the RDRAM buffer's actual size anywhere in this call chain**. Cross-referenced the crash-adjacent log: `[fb-get] REFUSE #40 addr=0x00FF3EC0 w=225 h=158 siz=2 oob=1` fired ~1300 lines before the crash (same tick). The math confirms an exact match: `rangeEnd = 0x00FF3EC0 + imageRowBytes(225)*158 ≈ 0x1005CFC`, roughly 8MB past the RDRAM buffer's actual 8MB (`0x800000`) size — reading that far past the buffer's end is exactly the kind of access that SIGBUSes.

**This is a real, previously-uncharacterized gap in s78's `FramebufferManager::get()` refuse gate**: that gate (rightly) keeps a wild-width/OOB-address FB request out of `framebuffers[]`, but it still **returns a `refuseFb` populated with the same wild `width`/`height`/`address` the caller asked for**, with only `readHeight` forced to 0 — the s78 comment explains this was needed to avoid a different assert (`copyRenderTargetToNative`), but it means any downstream consumer that doesn't know the FB was refused (here: `State::fullSync`'s `if (colorFb->height > colorFb->readHeight)` / depth's mirror block) still treats it as a normal, readable framebuffer and reads `&RDRAM[storageAddress]` for `readFbBytes` bytes — with wild dimensions, that read runs off the end of the 8MB RDRAM buffer.

**Fix landed** (`lib/rt64/src/hle/rt64_state.cpp`, both the color block at ~2222-2254 and the mirrored depth block at ~2284-2312): before calling `workload.fbStorage.store(...)`, compute `rangeEnd = storageAddress + readFbBytes` and skip the store/read (logging `[fbsync-oob-skip] color|depth #%d addr=... bytes=...`, same throttled-log pattern as `[fb-get] REFUSE`) if `storageAddress >= 0x800000 || rangeEnd > 0x800000`, reusing s78's `FramebufferManager::get()` 8MB constant. `colorFb->readHeight`/`depthFb->readHeight` are still advanced to `height` either way, so a skipped read doesn't get retried every tick. Pure `lib/rt64` host C++, no guest regen needed — rebuilt clean (`cmake --build`, only pre-existing imgui/SDL2-version warnings).

**Validated with one soak (`schedguard3`, identical env block/tag-bumped copy of `schedguard2`).** Positive control: `[fbsync-oob-skip]` fired **17/17** (color+depth combined), and — critically — **the exact crash that killed `schedguard2` at hold-iter 1 did not recur**; the process survived past that site and progressed further (`decisionN=8016` at death vs. `7734` in `schedguard2`, hold-iter 3 vs. hold-iter 1) before dying to a **different, already-catalogued** crash: a SIGSEGV entirely inside Apple's Metal shader-compiler internals (`MTLCompilerFSCache`/`MultiLevelAirCache`, no source on our side) — the same RT64-internal-with-no-source-on-our-side class first seen s83 and s96, not a new bug, not fixable at our level. `thr-resume bad=1: 0`, `UnhandledJump: 0`, `missing-func: 0` all held clean.

**Rules out:** "the s78 refuse gate alone is sufficient to make wild FB requests harmless" — it is not; any call site that reads a `Framebuffer`'s dimensions to pull bytes from RDRAM needs its own bounds check, independent of whether the FB ever entered `framebuffers[]`. Confirms the general "wild/OOB FB" bug family (s72/s78) has more than one downstream consumer that needs guarding — this is the first one found and fixed outside the original writeback/tilecopy paths.

**Still open:** the target stall itself. Both `schedguard2` and `schedguard3` died before `[thr-resume-skip]` could fire even once, so s180's "2nd independent confirmation" of the scheduler silent-drop mechanism is still outstanding — this session's fix removes one specific early-crash competitor but the Metal-internal SIGSEGV (non-deterministic per s83/s96, sometimes doesn't recur) is now the nearest remaining obstacle before the repro can reach the stall region again.

**Full detail**: this entry. Code: `lib/rt64/src/hle/rt64_state.cpp` (both read-into-storage blocks) — patch exported (`submodule-patches/rt64.patch`) + committed this session. Soak artifacts: `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/schedguard2/` and `schedguard3/` (run.log, screenshots), driver summaries `scratch/agent/schedguard{2,3}_driver.log`, driver scripts `scratch/agent/run_schedguard{2,3}.sh`.

Re-attempt the same soak shape 1-2 more times before considering that crash itself worth a characterization pass (it has no source on our side, so a fix there isn't possible — only working around it by understanding what triggers the shader compile, e.g. a first-time-seen material/shader combination in the hangar scene, is).
2. Try to land a 6th `rdpFs`-onset data point (any soak) to further tighten the ~3500-3800 ceiling band (now: 3560/3561/3784/3740/3747, unchanged this session — neither soak reached that phase).

## Session 183 (2026-07-28) — 4th `schedcaller` attempt reached AND SUSTAINED the target stall for the first time (hold-iter 68 vs. previous best 3), but `[thr-resume-skip]` fired 0 times the entire run — weakens, does not confirm, s180's scheduler-silent-drop mechanism as the (sole) cause

Per NEXT.md's step 1, re-ran the `schedcaller`-shape soak again (`schedguard4`, verbatim copy of `run_schedguard3.sh` except the tag, same env block/`STICK_SCHEDULE`). Goal: get past the non-deterministic Metal-internal SIGSEGV that killed `schedguard3` and reach the sustained stall with `[thr-create-id]`/`thr=%p` armed, then cross-reference a `[thr-resume-skip]` firing's `thr=%p` against `[thr-create-id]` to identify the dropped thread (NEXT.md step 2).

**Big jump in reach.** `schedguard4` survived to **hold-iter 68** (wall=75s into the 120s hold) — the deepest any soak in this line has gotten, vs. `schedguard3`'s hold-iter 3, `schedguard2`'s hold-iter 1, `schedguard1`'s ~7s. `fs max: 4010`, a new high (past the previously-tracked "~3500-3800 candidate ceiling" band from s176-179/s181/s182 — see below, that framing is refined this session, not just extended).

**Reached and sustained the actual target stall.** `[vi-fs-decision]` shows a clean, long, uninterrupted plateau: decisions **#9792 through #12480** (2688 decisions logged, the tail ~389 of them at the exact same `rdpFs=4010`) all read `SKIP reason=pair=0 seen=0 addrCh=0 stalled=1 pairs=0` — the canonical sustained-stall signature from s176-182, held far longer than any prior soak reached it. The crash's own `[CRASH][vifs-snapshot]` line confirms it structurally: `decisionN=12490 lastFireDecisionN=9770 decisionsSinceFire=2720 lastFireWasStalled=0 stalledNow=1` — the process was crashing *while inside* the stall, not before reaching it.

**Died to a new-looking crash, still inside the stall, with zero `[thr-resume-skip]` fires anywhere in the run.** SIGBUS (signal 10) inside `rs_free` (`funcs_0.c:3093`), called from `rebuildActiveDisplayObjectList` → `static_5_800C9BF0` → `menuOverlayInit` → `mainGameLoop` → `mainBootstrapWorker`. This is the same **shared-heap-corruption walker family** already catalogued (s164's 22nd class was `rs_malloc` ← the same `rebuildActiveDisplayObjectList` caller with sane-looking args; s167's 24th class was `rs_free` ← a different caller, `freeManifestSegmentAssets`) — this exact `rs_free ← rebuildActiveDisplayObjectList` combination hadn't been logged before, but it's a new data point *within* an existing family, not a new independent bug class.

**This is the key finding, and it cuts against s180's mechanism, not for it.** `grep -c "thr-resume-skip" run.log` → **0**, for the entire ~120s run, despite the process reaching, sustaining (2688 decisions), and eventually dying inside the exact stall region s180 characterized. s180's single prior occurrence found `[thr-resume-skip] tag=run_next id=0 ... bad_total=1` firing immediately before that run's stall onset, and framed it as *the* root cause. This run's stall onset — pinned tightly between decision `#9770` (last `FIRE reason=swap`) and `#9792` (first `SKIP ... stalled=1`), i.e. within ~22 decisions / a few hundred ms, same "tightly-timed" character as s180's finding — has **no scheduler bad-resume event anywhere near it**. Checked the raw log window between those two decisions directly (`sed -n '3862860,3866000p' run.log`, tag-filtered): the **only** non-heap-walk log line in that entire window is the `#9770 FIRE` line itself — no `[lle task]`, `[swap-ack-wait]`, `[thr-resume]`, or `[thr-resume-skip]` activity at all, consistent with s178's "the producer simply stops being invoked, no wait/yield, no error" characterization, but with a producer-stoppage this time that the s84 UAF-guard-skip mechanism cannot explain (it never fired).

**Refines (does not simply extend) the "rdpFs candidate shared ceiling" framing from s176-179/s181/s182.** rdpFs did **not** freeze exactly when the stall began — it climbed steadily to 3999, jumped to 4010 at decision `#9144`, and then **swaps kept firing normally for 626 more decisions** (`#9144`→`#9770`, all `FIRE reason=swap`, `stalled=0`, `rdpFs` pinned at 4010 the whole time) before the actual stall (no more FIREs at all) began at `#9792`. So "rdpFs stops incrementing" and "the graphics-task stall" are **two distinct events, not one** — rdpFs plateaus wherever the RDP opcode stream happens to end for this content, and normal swap/present activity continues for a while after that using the last-submitted content, before the *actual* stall (task submission itself stopping) hits separately, hundreds of decisions later. The specific plateau value (4010 here vs. 3560/3561/3784/3740/3747 previously) is content-dependent, not a fixed hang ceiling — tracking it further as a "ceiling to tighten" (open item 2, prior sessions) is not a productive framing; retiring that framing this session.

**Rules out:** "the s84 `[thr-resume-skip]` scheduler silent-drop is a necessary precondition for this stall" as a general claim — it is sufficient in at least one observed instance (s180) but **not necessary** in at least one other (this session), since the stall was reached, sustained, and crashed-through with zero occurrences of that log line. Does not rule out that s180's occurrence was still a real, valid instance of *a* cause of the stall — multiple independent mechanisms landing on the same externally-observed symptom (`[vi-fs-decision] stalled=1 pairs=0` sustained) is now the better-supported framing than "one root cause".

**Not chased further this session** (per rule 8 posture — this is a discriminating result, not a null, so the right move is to write it up and re-plan, not keep soaking blind): what specifically stops `[lle task]`/`[swap-ack-wait]` being invoked in *this* run's `#9770`→`#9792` window, if not the s84 UAF guard. That is now the open question item -33 was trying to answer, reopened with a refuted leading hypothesis.

**Full detail**: this entry. No code changes this session (pure re-run of existing instruments, no `lib/` edits — `export.sh` not needed). Soak artifacts: `scratch/s73_post_a_scene/schedguard4/` (run.log — 1.7GB, screenshots through `hold_67.png`), driver summary `scratch/agent/schedguard4_driver.log`, driver scripts `scratch/agent/run_schedguard4.sh`/`wait_for_schedguard4.sh`.

Candidates to check by source-read first (per rule 5, before instrumenting): (a) the outer hangar-tick loop's own exit/break conditions (s180 already confirmed *a* version of "outer loop stops iterating" — re-check whether that's reachable without going through `resume_thread_tagged`'s bad-context branch at all, e.g. a normal/successful thread switch that simply never switches back); (b) `viRetraceHandlerThread`/`musyxSynthFrame`'s per-VI-retrace tick — does it, or some audio-side blocking call, ever hold a lock or resource the graphics-task producer needs; (c) whether `[rs-malloc-walk]`/`[rs-free-walk]` volume itself (they dominate the log almost totally during and after the stall) points at a heap-exhaustion or allocation-stall condition on the producer's own allocation path. Keep `[thr-create-id]`/`thr=%p` armed regardless (free, no rebuild) in case a *different* run's stall onset does correlate with a `[thr-resume-skip]` fire — s180's mechanism is weakened as a general explanation, not eliminated as *a* possible one.

## Session 184 (2026-07-28) — source-read confirmed candidate (a) is mechanistically real (a strict priority-greater-than scheduler gate can strand a low-priority thread), landed and validated a scheduler-decision instrument to test it; one soak died before reaching the stall region to a distinct, previously-uncatalogued SIGBUS signature inside `evalCubicSplineAtTime`

### Work unit
NEXT.md step 1: source-read the three -35 candidates before instrumenting. Read
`lib/N64ModernRuntime/ultramodern/src/threads.cpp` (`resume_thread_tagged`,
`run_next_thread`, `run_next_thread_and_wait`) and `scheduling.cpp`
(`schedule_running_thread`, `swap_to_thread`, `check_running_queue`,
`pause_self`/`yield_self`) end to end, plus `mesgqueue.cpp`'s `do_send`/`do_recv`
blocking paths.

### Finding: two structurally different "who runs next" mechanisms exist, and only one is priority-blind
- `check_running_queue()` (called after every non-blocking `osSendMesg`/
  `osJamMesg`/`osRecvMesg`, `osSetThreadPri`, `osStartThread`) only swaps to the
  head of `running_queue` if `next_thread->priority > self->priority` —
  **strictly greater**. A tie or a lower-priority queued thread is left
  queued, untouched, and the function returns silently.
- `run_next_thread()` (reached only via `run_next_thread_and_wait`, itself only
  called from `do_send`/`do_recv`'s **blocking** loops in `mesgqueue.cpp` and
  from `osStopThread`'s self-stop path, and from `_thread_func`'s natural-exit
  path) pops `running_queue` **unconditionally**, ignoring priority entirely.
- Consequence: a thread queued into `running_queue` via `schedule_running_thread`
  (the wake-a-blocked-thread path in `do_send`/`do_recv`) is only guaranteed to
  run again if *some* thread, at some point, executes a genuine blocking wait
  (hitting the unconditional pop) — never-preempting priority comparisons alone
  cannot resume it if every thread that subsequently calls
  `check_running_queue` has priority ≥ the queued thread's.
- Checked this against real data already on disk from s183's `schedguard4/`
  run.log (`[thr-create-id]` lines, no new soak needed): `mainBootstrapWorker`
  (thread id=3, entry `0x80000C68` — the hangar-loop/graphics-task-producer
  thread per s93) is created at **priority 10**, one of the lowest of any
  active thread in the roster; `viRetraceHandlerThread` (entry `0x80019868`)
  runs at **priority 117**, and the three audio-related id=0 threads
  (entries `0x8001C328`/`0x80019BF4`/`0x8008ED70`, the last confirmed s70/71
  as `runAiAudioStreamPlaybackLoop`) run at **117-122**. This is exactly the
  priority shape the mechanism needs: if thread 3 is ever queued by a
  non-blocking send/recv from one of these ≥117-priority threads, and none of
  them subsequently performs a genuine blocking wait, thread 3 stays parked
  with **zero** `resume_thread_tagged` activity of any kind — matching s183's
  "0 `thr-resume-skip`, 0 resume activity near the stall" observation exactly,
  and doing so **without needing the s84 UAF guard to fire at all**.

### Instrument landed (`lib/N64ModernRuntime`, pure host C++, no guest/fixup changes)
`ROGUESQ_LOG_SCHED=1` (new env gate, mirrors `ROGUESQ_LOG_THREAD_RESUME`'s
cached-getenv pattern; **not** always-on because both call sites are hot —
`check_running_queue` and `run_next_thread` run on every message send/recv,
same class of hot path s93 found perturbs timing when logged verbosely):
- `scheduling.cpp` `schedule_running_thread`: `[sched-queue] thr=%p id=%d
  pri=%d` — every time a thread is queued into `running_queue`.
- `scheduling.cpp` `check_running_queue`: `[sched-check] self_thr=%p
  self_id=%d self_pri=%d head_thr=%p head_id=%d head_pri=%d swap=%d` — only
  inside the already-existing `!thread_queue_empty()` branch, so it does not
  fire on the common (queue-empty) case.
- `threads.cpp` `run_next_thread`: `[sched-runnext] popped_thr=%p popped_id=%d
  popped_pri=%d` — every unconditional pop.
Patch exported (`./submodule-patches/export.sh` — only
`submodule-patches/N64ModernRuntime.patch` changed, `rt64.patch` untouched)
and committed this session. Built clean via `cmake --build build`
(`DEVELOPER_DIR=/Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer`), 0 errors, only
pre-existing SDL2-compat linker version warnings.

### Soak (`schedguard5`, same env block as `schedguard3`/`schedguard4` plus `ROGUESQ_LOG_SCHED=1`)
Positive control fired: 72382 `[sched-queue]`, 333003 `[sched-check]`, 72380
`[sched-runnext]` lines. **Died at hold-iter 6** (`decisionN=8327`), well
*before* the `#9770`-`#9792`-equivalent stall-onset region s180/s183 both
reached (~decision 9770-9792) — this run never got far enough to test the
hypothesis directly. Death: **SIGBUS (signal 10)** inside `evalCubicSplineAtTime
+ 2552`, called from `buildPositionAndCallTransformHelper` →
`setupActorAnchorTransformType1` → `static_5_800AB658` → `static_5_800AAD9C` →
`static_5_800C6854` → `menuOverlayInit` → `mainGameLoop` →
`mainBootstrapWorker`. **This is not the s83-guarded crash** — s83's guard
targets a `NAN_CHECK` assert abort (signal 6/SIGABRT) at one specific
division site (`0x8001906C`); this is a bus error (signal 10, an out-of-bounds
memory access), a different signal and almost certainly a different fault
site within the same function, not previously catalogued under this name.
Not root-caused this session (would need its own source read — flagged, not
chased, per the "don't spend a soak chasing an unrelated crash" posture that
already applies to `rs_free`/`rebuildActiveDisplayObjectList`).

### What the pre-crash data does say (non-discriminating for -35, but not nothing)
In the ~8300 decisions before death, `[sched-queue]` (72382) and
`[sched-runnext]` (72380) counts are within 2 of each other — i.e. in normal
(non-stalled) operation, almost every thread that gets queued does
subsequently get an unconditional-pop chance; starvation via the strict
priority gate is **not** the routine case. This refines rather than confirms
the hypothesis: reaching the stall would require the unconditional-pop path
(`run_next_thread`) to stop firing *for any thread* right around the stall
onset — not a generic, ever-present race. The right discriminating check for
a future run that reaches the stall: does `[sched-runnext]` stop appearing
entirely in the window after the last `[sched-queue]` that names the producer
thread's `thr=` pointer.

### Rules out / keeps
- Keeps `ROGUESQ_LOG_SCHED` armed as a free addition for any future soak that
  reaches the stall region (same posture as `[thr-create-id]`).
- Does not rule in or out candidate (a) — inconclusive, this run didn't reach
  the target window. Not yet a 2nd or 3rd attempt on this specific
  instrument (rule 8 budget: 1 of up to 3 before re-planning).
- Surfaces a new, distinct SIGBUS signature in `evalCubicSplineAtTime`
  (signal 10, offset +2552) as a competing early-death risk for any future
  soak attempting to reach the stall region, alongside the already-catalogued
  Metal-internal SIGSEGV and the `rs_free`/heap-corruption family.

   does it get a `[sched-queue]` entry with no subsequent `[sched-check

2. Candidates (b) (`viRetraceHandlerThread`/`musyxSynthFrame` lock/resource

## Session 187 (2026-07-28) — landed the mandatory-pivot defensive guard on `rs_free`'s free-list walk (3 loops, `N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`), positive control fired 1901x on ONE persistent corrupted node, and the soak survived the ENTIRE 120s hold + grace window with zero crashes — first fully crash-free full-length run anywhere in the s180-187 `schedcaller`/`schedguard`/`rsfreeguard` lineage

### What ran
Per NEXT.md's mandatory pivot (s186 closed the `ROGUESQ_LOG_SCHED` rule-8
budget at 3/3 inconclusive): source-read `rs_free`
(`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_0.c:3106`, confirmed itself a
`RECOMP_FUNC` — a single shared guest function, so a guard inside it covers
every caller including `rebuildActiveDisplayObjectList` (s183/s186) and
`freeManifestSegmentAssets` (s167/s185) at once). Found `rs_free` contains
**3 near-identical coalescing free-list walk loops**
(`L_80001CE0`/`L_80001DCC`/`L_80001EB4`), each computing
`next = node + size_field` with **zero bounds checking anywhere in the
recomp memory macros** (`N64Recomp/include/recomp.h`'s `MEM_W`/`MEM_HU` do
raw pointer arithmetic into the `rdram` buffer, no clamp) and then
dereferencing through that computed address a few instructions later. s186's
own `[rs-free-walk]` log had already shown the shape: `node=0x80160120
flags=0x0 size=2155119224` — a garbage size that overflows the node's
address 27 MB past the 8 MB RDRAM window (`ram_size = 0x800000`,
`lib/N64ModernRuntime/librecomp/src/sp.cpp:23`), guaranteeing a wild
dereference on the very next access.

Landed a guard (mirroring the s173 `rs_malloc` walk-loop-deref-guard
precedent exactly: same `0x80000000u`/`0x80800000u` RDRAM bounds, same
`goto` to the loop's own natural "terminator bit already set" exit label
instead of continuing to dereference) at all 3 walk loops, gated by a
single new env var `ROGUESQ_LOG_RS_FREE_WALK_GUARD`, logging
`[rs-free-walk-guard] loop=<1|2|3> n=<fire count> bad_next=<addr>
node=<addr> ra=<addr>` on trip. Loop 1's bail target is `L_80001D94`, loop
2's is `L_80001E80`, loop 3's is `L_80001F64` (the function's own
lock-release-and-return tail) — each chosen to exactly match that loop's
existing "list search ends here" control-flow shape, not skip any
additional coalescing work beyond what the real terminator path already
skips.

Regenerated fresh (`N64Recomp` was NOT re-run on an already-patched
`funcs_0.c` — regenerated from the ELF first per the non-idempotency rule,
then `fixup_game_funcs.py` once): fixup log confirms all 3 new patches at
exactly x1 (`funcs_0.c: rs_free free-list walk-loop deref guard loop{1,2,3}
patched x1`), plus the pre-existing s140/s168 rs_free patches also at x1
each (no duplication). Built clean
(`DEVELOPER_DIR=.../Xcode.app/... cmake --build build`).

One soak (`rsfreeguard1`, same env block as `run_schedguard7.sh` plus
`ROGUESQ_LOG_RS_FREE_WALK_GUARD=1`, `ROGUESQ_LOG_SCHED=1` kept armed): the
process **survived the entire 120s hold window + 0s grace and had to be
killed manually** (`game process still alive; killing`) — `CRASH: 0` in the
driver summary. `[rs-free-walk-guard]` fired **1901 times**, all
`loop=1`, all on the exact same node/corruption pair
(`node=0x807982B6 bad_next=0x8475841C`) — a single persistently-corrupted
free-list node that `rs_free` re-encounters on every single call for the
rest of the run, now safely bailed every time instead of crashing on
(what must have been, pre-guard) an eventual unlucky hit. `[sched-queue]`/
`[sched-runnext]`: 131076/131075 — near-balanced, consistent with s184-186.

### Rules out / keeps
- **This specific `rs_free` free-list-walk corruption family (killed s183,
  s185, s186 — 3 of the last 4 scheduling-line attempts) is now defended
  against at its walk site.** Positive control is unambiguous: 1901 fires
  in one run, process did not crash. This is a local guard (buying
  runway), NOT a fix for the underlying corruption that puts the insane
  size value in the free list in the first place — that chase (s85-s114)
  is still open and this session did not touch it.
- **New data point for that still-open corruption chase, not investigated
  further this session**: unlike s173's `rs_malloc` guard (corruption
  proved racy across runs — 0/0 fires with 17,683 clean calls one run),
  this `rs_free` corruption looks **deterministic within a run once it
  occurs** — the same node/bad_next pair fired on essentially every `rs_free`
  call for the remainder of the soak (1901x), not a rare one-off. Worth
  keeping in mind if/when the corruption-source chase resumes: this
  particular node persists in the free list rather than being cleaned up
  or re-corrupted differently each time.
- **Did not observe or rule out the `-35` stall itself this run.** The
  crash-only `[CRASH][vifs-snapshot] decisionN=...` counter is the only
  place `ROGUESQ_LOG_SCHED`'s decision number gets printed — with no
  crash this run, there is no decision-number readout at all, so we cannot
  tell whether this run passed through, sustained, or never reached the
  historical stall window. `[sched-queue]`/`[sched-runnext]` staying
  near-balanced for the whole run is at least consistent with "never
  stalled," matching s183/s186's balanced-until-the-crash pattern, but is
  not itself proof either way. **Instrumentation gap for next session**:
  a periodic (not just crash-time) `decisionN` log line would let a
  crash-free run like this one actually report whether it stalled.

### Carried-forward open items

1. **Add a periodic (non-crash-gated) `[sched-decision]`-style log tick**
   (e.g. every N decisions, or on a wall-clock timer) so a crash-free run
   can report whether/when it hit the `-35` stall, since this session's
   guard just produced the first crash-free run in the lineage and it went
   fully "dark" on that specific question. This unblocks re-testing
   candidate (a) (`ROGUESQ_LOG_SCHED`'s own hypothesis, rule-8 budget
   closed for *dedicated* attempts but the flag itself is still armed and

2. Candidates (b) (`viRetraceHandlerThread`/`musyxSynthFrame` lock/resource
   contention) and (c) (heap-exhaustion on the producer's allocation path)
   remain unexamined.
3. `evalCubicSplineAtTime+2552` SIGBUS (s184, signal 10) — still not root-
   caused, still not recurred a 2nd time.
4. `tickSongSequence`'s 2 unguarded list walks (funcs_25.c:5018-5046,
   5050-5077, found s174) — still open.
5. `submitSceneNodeRender+16780` (s171) — still open, still lowest priority.
6. The underlying `rs_free`-corruption source (what writes the insane size
   into node `0x807982B6`'s free-list header in the first place) is still
   unlocated — this session's guard treats the symptom, not the cause.

## Session 190 (2026-07-28) — corrected a documentation error in s189's "4 existing guards on processSceneNode" claim (only 1 of the 4 actually touches that function), landed the missing node-pointer guard, caught and fixed a self-introduced regression via a control-run comparison, then hit a different, already-catalogued crash before reaching the target decision window

**Correction before doing anything else**: NEXT.md/CURRENT-TRUTH item -38 said
`N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py` carries "4 guards on this exact function
(`processSceneNode`)" and that none of them fired in `schedtick1`. Cross-
referencing guest addresses (not just guard names) against the function
boundaries (`grep -n "^RECOMP_FUNC" funcs_4.c`) shows this was wrong: 3 of the
4 (`_scene_node_list_guard_patch`/`_guard2`/`_guard3`, fixup script lines
~2337-2478) are patched into **`submitSceneNodeRender`** (funcs_4.c:6-2999,
guest ~0x8000FEA0-0x800112xx) — a completely different function that guards
its own free-list allocator walk and is not even in this crash's call stack.
Only s175's recursion-depth cap (fixup script lines ~3899-3990) actually
touches `processSceneNode` (funcs_4.c:13759-14879), and it only counts calls —
it never validates the node pointer itself. So the interior of
`processSceneNode` had **zero** real deref guards, not 3, before this session.
This doesn't overturn s189's core finding (the crash is one specific unguarded
dereference, not a depth phenomenon) but it does mean the "none of 4 guards
fired" evidence was 4x weaker than it looked — only 1 of the citations was
actually a relevant null result.

**Source-read** (`processSceneNode`/`traverseSceneGraphRecursive`,
funcs_4.c:13759-15184, building on s175's own groundwork comment) found the
mechanism NEXT.md asked for: `traverseSceneGraphRecursive` walks a sibling
list rooted at mutable global `0x80112B20`, reading each node's own "next"
field at offset 0 with zero bounds checking (funcs_4.c:15073-15074,
`ctx->r3 = MEM_W(ctx->r3, 0X0)`), then passes that same raw pointer straight
into the recursive `processSceneNode(rdram, ctx)` call as its `a2` argument
— which becomes `processSceneNode`'s own node pointer (`ctx->r17`/$s1,
funcs_4.c:13766-13767) and is dereferenced immediately on entry
(funcs_4.c:13792 pre-patch, `MEM_W(ctx->r17, 0XC)`) with no validation
anywhere in between. A single corrupted "next" field anywhere in the sibling
chain flows straight through the recursive-call boundary into a raw
dereference — explaining the fixed native-offset SIGBUS across independent
recurrences/rebuilds without needing a depth-overflow explanation.

**Fix landed**: a new entry-point guard on `processSceneNode`'s node pointer
(`ctx->r17`), checked once right after s175's depth cap and before the first
dereference, bailing to the same `L_80015528` exit with the same `ctx->r2=0`
sentinel the caller's sibling-loop condition already reads as "stop
iterating this level" (`N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`, new
`ROGUESQ_LOG_SCENE_NODE_PTR_GUARD` env var, `[scene-node-ptr-guard]` log
tag). Full regen (`make_elf.py` not needed, only fixup script changed →
`regen_n64recomp.sh` → `fixup_game_funcs.py` once, confirmed `x1` for the new
patch and all 3 pre-existing `processSceneNode`-adjacent patches still `x1`,
no duplication) → `cmake --build`, exit 0, only pre-existing-class warnings.

**Caught and fixed a self-introduced regression before it could contaminate
the result** (this is itself the most reusable finding this session): the
first version of the patch's regex match consumed the pre-existing
`ctx->r3 = MEM_W(ctx->r17, 0XC);` line as a stable anchor but the replacement
function never re-emitted it, silently **deleting that instruction** from
the compiled function. Two soaks on that build (`sceneptrguard1`,
`sceneptrguard2`, same env block as s188's `schedtick1` plus the new guard's
env var) both crashed **immediately and byte-identically** at
decisionN=151/149 — a brand-new signature never seen before
(`submitSceneNodeRender+2156` self-call, called from `processSceneNode`,
never a scene the game had reached this early in any prior soak) — with the
new guard's own log tag **never firing** (0/0), which was the tell: the
guard's mere presence, not its activation, was changing behavior, pointing
at a codegen bug rather than a triggered false-positive. Built and ran a
control (`controlnoguard1`): identical env block, only the new patch
disabled (temporarily neutered via `if False and p.name == ...`) — survived
the **entire 120s hold + grace window with zero crashes**, decisionN reached
14721+ before being killed manually. That confirmed the regression was
caused by the patch itself, not the pre-existing lib state, and pointed
straight at the deleted deref line once the diff was re-examined. Fixed by
re-appending the original line to the replacement string; regenerated,
confirmed `x1` again, rebuilt.

**Post-fix soak (`sceneptrguard3`)**: no regression — decisionN climbed
cleanly through a real VI-width transition (1024→512, a legitimate mission
load, not a crash) to **8053** before dying to a SIGBUS in
`reserveAndEmitDLEntry` (called via `submitSceneNodeRender` ←
`processSceneNode` ← `traverseSceneGraphRecursive` (twice, +1576/+2336) ←
`setupCameraMatrices` ← ...). This is the **already-catalogued 14th class**
(`reserveAndEmitDLEntry`, first identified s168-171, PORTING-STATE ~15574-
15780) recurring at a native offset (+5212) past both the s109 guard and the
3 guards s169 added — a whack-a-mole-shaped "another unguarded deref in the
same function" recurrence, not a new bug family. **`scene-node-ptr-guard`
did not fire** (0) — meaning this run never reached a call where the node
pointer was actually corrupted, so **the guard's effectiveness against the
target processSceneNode self-recursion bug (9660-9800 decisionN window) is
still untested** — the run was blocked by a different, earlier crash before
it could get there.

### Result

1. Corrected CURRENT-TRUTH item -38: only 1 of the "4 existing guards" is
   actually on `processSceneNode`; the other 3 guard an unrelated function
   (`submitSceneNodeRender`).
2. Landed `ROGUESQ_LOG_SCENE_NODE_PTR_GUARD` on `processSceneNode`'s node
   pointer (`N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`, funcs_4.c entry, mirrors the
   depth-cap's bail semantics).
3. Found, root-caused, and fixed a self-introduced regression (deleted
   instruction from an over-greedy regex match) using a same-session control
   build as the discriminating test — 2/2 crash with the bug, 1/1 crash-free
   past decisionN 14721+ with the same patch disabled.
4. The actual target question (does the fixed guard let decisionN push past
   9792, and does the `-35` stall signature appear) is **still open** — this
   run hit a different, already-catalogued crash (`reserveAndEmitDLEntry`,
   14th class) at decisionN=8053 first. Not evidence against the fix; just
   an earlier obstacle in the same run.

No `submodule-patches/export.sh` needed — all edits this session were in the
standalone `N64Recomp` tool checkout (`fixup_game_funcs.py`,
`RecompiledFuncs/*.c` regenerated output) and `RogueSquadron64Recomp/scratch/
agent/*`, nothing under `RogueSquadron64Recomp/lib/`.

`otool -tv -p` and `objdump --disassemble-symbols=` against
`build/RogueSquadron64Recomp`, as ordinary non-piped Bash calls. Both

blocked, don't burn budget re-attempting"), did not retry a 3rd time and
did not touch `s193_disasm.py` (still unvalidated, still not trusted).

**Pivot: the crash handler was silently discarding its own best evidence.**
Reading the existing POSIX signal handler
(`src/main/main.cpp:1654-1683`) to plan the decoder-validation sub-step
turned up a cheaper, more reliable path: it installs with `SA_SIGINFO`
(`sa.sa_flags = SA_SIGINFO | SA_RESETHAND`) but the handler lambda was
`[](int sig, siginfo_t*, void*)` — both the `siginfo_t*` (has `si_addr`,
the exact faulting virtual address) and the `void*` `ucontext_t*` (has the
full ARM64 register file: `x0`-`x28`, `fp`, `lr`, `sp`, `pc`, `cpsr`, plus
`__es.__far`/`__esr`/`__exception`, all inside `uc_mcontext->__ss`/`__es`
on Darwin/arm64) were being discarded. This is strictly better than
disassembly for identifying a bad-pointer crash: instead of inferring which
register held the bad value from the instruction encoding, the register
file at the exact fault instant is just... there, already captured by the
kernel, for free. No new build risk beyond the crash path itself (all other
code paths unaffected).

**Change:** `src/main/main.cpp` — added `#include <sys/ucontext.h>` (not
`<ucontext.h>`, which requires `_XOPEN_SOURCE` on this SDK and errored:
"deprecated ucontext routines require _XOPEN_SOURCE to be defined"; the
BSD-style `<sys/ucontext.h>` header exposes the same `ucontext_t`/
`mcontext_t` struct layout without that guard). Extended the lambda to
print `[CRASH][siginfo] si_addr=... si_code=... si_errno=...` and, on
`__APPLE__ && __aarch64__`, `[CRASH][mcontext] pc=... far=... esr=...
exception=...` followed by all 29 `x` registers and `fp`/`lr`/`sp`/`cpsr`.
Pure `src/main/main.cpp` change (this repo, not `lib/`) — built with a
plain `cmake --build build --target RogueSquadron64Recomp -j`, no
regen/fixup pipeline needed, builds clean (2 pre-existing unrelated
deprecation warnings in `rt64`'s vendored `json.hpp`, nothing new).

**Soak (`scratch/agent/run_mcontext1.sh`, tag `mcontext1`, identical env
block to s192/s193's `sceneptrguard5`): the new dump fired, gave a sane,
internally-consistent read, and the run reached the furthest decisionN of
any soak to date.** `CRASH: 34` in the summary (many are the routine
already-catalogued small crashes this soak script's env block doesn't
guard against; the interesting one is the fatal one that ended the run):

```
[CRASH] caught signal 10 (Bus error: 10), dumping stack:
[CRASH][siginfo] si_addr=0x380630062 si_code=1 si_errno=0
[CRASH][mcontext] pc=0x1028cc4a4 far=0x380630062 esr=0x92000006 exception=0x0
[CRASH][mcontext] x0 =0x0000000300000000   (== x8; almost certainly the rdram host base pointer)
[CRASH][mcontext] x8 =0x0000000300000000
[CRASH][mcontext] x9 =0x0000000080630062   (raw, UNSIGN-EXTENDED KSEG0 guest pointer)
... (x1-x7, x10-x28 mostly small/zero, not implicated)
[CRASH][mcontext] fp=0x000000016fe628c0 lr=0x00000001028ee4fc sp=0x000000016fe62890 cpsr=0xa0000000
[CRASH][vifs-snapshot] decisionN=9741 lastFireDecisionN=9740 decisionsSinceFire=1 lastFireWasStalled=0 stalledNow=0
3   RogueSquadron64Recomp   0x00000001028ee4fc processSceneNode + 8772
5   RogueSquadron64Recomp   0x00000001028ef910 traverseSceneGraphRecursive + 1576
```
(`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/mcontext1/run.log:4468133-4468166`)

**Reading the register file directly identifies the bug class, no
disassembly needed:** `far` (== `si_addr`, self-consistent) decomposes
exactly as `x0/x8 (0x300000000) + x9 (0x80630062)` — the host rdram base
pointer plus a guest pointer that STILL HAS its KSEG0 tag (`0x80000000`)
intact and is zero-extended (upper 32 bits of x9 are 0), not sign-extended.
Compare `N64Recomp/include/recomp.h`'s `MEM_W` macro (the normal/correct
path): `rdram + ((reg + offset) - 0xFFFFFFFF80000000)`, which only works
because `ADD32` sign-extends 32-bit register values through `(gpr)(int32_t)(...)`
to `0xFFFFFFFF80xxxxxx` before the macro subtracts the KSEG0 base. Here,
whatever computed this address added the RAW, zero-extended 32-bit guest
value directly to the rdram base with NO KSEG0 subtraction at all — a
different, less-safe code path than `MEM_W`, producing an ~2 GB wild
pointer instead of a valid ~8 MB rdram offset. This is a genuinely new
mechanism, distinct from every previously-catalogued crash in this
project's history (none of which were characterized as a masking/sign-
extension bug before). `lr=processSceneNode+8772` is the RETURN address of
a call from inside `processSceneNode` (`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_4.c:13759-14873`)
to whatever's at the actual faulting `pc` — the unwinder couldn't resolve a
symbol for `pc` itself (likely a small/leaf helper with no separate frame),
which is why the backtrace shows the caller. **Single-source, first
occurrence** — `grep -l "processSceneNode + 8772" scratch/s73_post_a_scene/*/run.log`
matches only this run; not yet confirmed as a recurring crash class the
way `queueGPUUploadTMEM`/`rs_malloc` are.

**Milestone: furthest decisionN yet, and it's INSIDE the target window.**
Prior furthest was s192's 8972; this soak reached 9741, past the
`[scene-node-ptr-guard]` target window's start (9660) and still short of
its end (9792). `[scene-node-ptr-guard]` fired 0 times again (now 0/4
across all soaks) — this NEW crash killed the run before the guarded site
could be exercised, so the s190 fix is STILL untested, but the accumulated
guards from s190-s193 are demonstrably doing their job: this is the first
soak to ever get this deep. Did not attempt to pinpoint the exact source
statement or add a guard this session — that's real, separate, bounded
work (need to identify which call site inside `processSceneNode` passes an
unmasked pointer, most likely by finding a place that skips `MEM_W`/`ADD32`
and does raw pointer arithmetic) and this session's actual deliverable
(the mcontext instrument) is already a complete, validated, standalone
unit. Two runs is not enough to know if this crash is itself the new
soak-blocking bottleneck or a one-off; that's the natural next probe.

**What this does and doesn't show:**
- DOES confirm the new `[CRASH][siginfo]`/`[CRASH][mcontext]` dump is live,

- DOES identify a real, previously-invisible bug MECHANISM (KSEG0-tagged

### What ran

Per NEXT.md, delegated a full source-read of `submitSceneNodeRender`
(`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_4.c:6-2999`) to a subagent to find an
unguarded pointer-chase not covered by the existing GUARD/GUARD2/GUARD3
(s123/s131). It returned 6 ranked candidates; verified candidate #1 by hand
(funcs_4.c:179-306, the free-list-push/pop sequence) and found the REAL
gap, more precise than the agent's framing: at `0x8001014C`
(`bne $a0,$zero,L_800101AC`), if the persistent global free-list cache
(`0x801163B0`) is non-zero at function entry, execution jumps straight to
`L_800101AC`, skipping `findAndUnlinkSmallestEntry` and all three existing
guards (which only protect the path taken when the cache is empty). At
`L_800101AC`/`0x800101B4` the reloaded cache pointer is dereferenced for the
first time with zero validation. This is structurally the SAME reason
GUARD/GUARD2/GUARD3 have fired 0/0 across 2 independent post-guard
recurrences (s131/s134) of the exact same crash signature (`+28208`): the
crash isn't in the part they guard, it's in the one dereference they can't
reach.

Landed the guard (`N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`, new function inserted
after the GUARD2/GUARD3 block, file-scoped to `funcs_4.c`, new env var
`ROGUESQ_LOG_SCENE_NODE_CACHE_GUARD`): checks the reloaded cache pointer for
RDRAM-range sanity before the deref; on failure, logs, resets the corrupt
global cache to 0 (so the NEXT call takes the `findAndUnlinkSmallestEntry`
path instead of re-hitting the same corrupt value forever — unlike the
other 3 guards' bail targets, simply re-jumping to the existing "empty
cache" reentry point here would immediately re-crash on the same corrupt
global, so this guard explicitly clears it), sets the local copy to 0 to
match, and jumps to `L_800101C8` — the same merge point the code's own
`r2==0` branch already reaches, no new code path invented.

Regenerated (`make_elf.py` -> `N64Recomp` -> `fixup_game_funcs.py`, verified

## Session 199 (2026-07-28) — added a source-level defensive guard on `runVideoFrameTick`'s 3 global video-state-pointer derefs (disassembly still blocked); 2 informative soaks show no recurrence of the `+1568` crash, but a 3rd soak's DEATH is itself the headline: a byte-for-byte 2nd occurrence of s194's single-occurrence `processSceneNode+8772` KSEG0-zero-extension bug, promoting it to the new top-priority confirmed-recurring crash

### Disassembly tooling: re-confirmed still blocked, did not retry further

Per NEXT.md step 1, tried `otool -tv build/RogueSquadron64Recomp` fresh this
session as a plain non-piped Bash call. Result: `"This command requires
approval"` — no human is present in this non-interactive session to clear
it, same outcome s193/s194 already established. Did not retry a 2nd time
(NEXT.md's own guidance) and did not touch the hand-rolled decoder
(`s193_disasm.py`, already shown untrustworthy). Went straight to step 2,
the broad defensive-guard fallback.

### What ran — the guard

A full read of `runVideoFrameTick` (`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_0.c:1459`,
the whole ~415-line/177-MIPS-instruction function, confirmed still exactly
this range) found the function's derefs fall into two clearly distinct
classes: the vast majority use pointers that come directly from the
function's own arguments (`$s3`/`$s0`/`$s2`, `ctx->r19`/`r16`/`r18`) —
exercised on literally every call across every soak this project has ever
run, with zero attributable crashes. But at 3 sites (MIPS
`0x8000154C`/`0x8000157C`/`0x800015BC`) the function instead LOADS A POINTER
FROM A FIXED GLOBAL RDRAM ADDRESS (`lui $v0,0x8011; lw $v0,-0x350($v0)` ==
guest `0x8010FCB0`) and immediately dereferences it via raw `MEM_W`/
`do_swl`/`do_swr` writes (offsets `0x10`-`0x44`) with zero validation — the
same "cached/global pointer, never checked" shape as every previously
guarded crash class in this project (s99, s100, s109, s169, s197's
`scene-node-cache-guard`). All 3 writes are gated behind a chain of
conditional branches upstream (`reapplyDisplayMode` returning 0, a byte flag
at `$s2+4`, etc.), so this global is exercised far less often than the rest
of the function — consistent with an intermittent, thousands-of-decisions-deep
crash rather than an every-call one.

Cross-checked against s198's own crash evidence: the s194 crash-handler
upgrade recorded `si_addr=0x320000000` for this exact `+1568` crash — many
GB past any valid rdram offset, the signature of an unmasked/garbage
pointer, not a near-miss. This matches the global-pointer hypothesis:
`MEM_W` (`N64Recomp/include/recomp.h`) is completely unbounded (
`rdram + ((reg+offset) - 0xFFFFFFFF80000000)`, no range check at all,
relies entirely on the register holding a correctly sign-extended
`0x80000000`-`0x807FFFFF` guest address) — if the global at `0x8010FCB0` is
ever 0/uninitialized/corrupt, the resulting host pointer lands wildly
outside the 8 MB rdram buffer.

Guarded all 3 sites (`N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`, `funcs_0.c`,
`ROGUESQ_LOG_VIDEO_FRAME_TICK_GUARD`): after each load, check the pointer is
in the valid RDRAM range; if not, log (env-gated) and skip ONLY that site's
reads+writes (confirmed by reading the surrounding code that every register
touched is freshly reloaded by the next site or the function epilogue — no
stale-value hazard from skipping). Unlike s197's cache guard, does NOT reset
the global to a known-safe value — its true semantics (likely a camera/
video-mode state struct, not a free-list head) aren't established, so
overwriting it could introduce a new bug; skip-only is the minimal,
defensible change. Full regen (`make_elf.py` → `N64Recomp` →
`fixup_game_funcs.py` → `cmake --build`) ran clean; verified the patch
applied exactly once per site (`grep -c "video-frame-tick-guard"
funcs_0.c` → 3, not 6). Pure `N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py` change (outside
this repo, flagged for the user per standing convention, not committed by
this session).
