## Session 249 (2026-07-28)

**Picked option 1 from s248's `NEXT.md` (project-wide static sweep for the
"RDRAM-base-constant + un-subtracted wild guest pointer" whack-a-mole
family) over option 2 (`CURRENT-TRUTH.md` housekeeping), since it's real
code and per `ITERATION.md` housekeeping alone doesn't count as
`ADVANCED`. Landed one new guard (`selectPostCrawlCraft`,
`funcs_30.c`) plus a reusable project-wide candidate-finder script; build
clean; 1 soak run showed no regression from the change and no new
information on whether the guarded site is actually hot.**

**Step 1 — grep the idiom shape project-wide, as NEXT.md's first step
asked.** The naive signature (self-referential `ctx->rX = MEM_W(ctx->rX,
0X0)`, matching heapWalker/heapFreeListDequeue's already-fixed shape) hits
794 times across the 45 `funcs_*.c` files — far too broad; most are
one-shot, already-bounded dereferences, not unguarded list-walk loops.
Narrowed with a script
(`scratch/agent/find_unguarded_walks.py`, output
`scratch/agent/unguarded_walk_candidates.json`) that requires the
self-ref load to sit at a labeled loop target which is the destination of
a **backward** `goto` (i.e. an actual loop back-edge, not just any
self-ref line) and have no existing `PATCH` guard already covering it.
This dropped the count to **143 candidate sites across 43 functions** —
still confirmed the exclusion logic works (heapWalker itself, already
fully guarded, correctly does not appear). Full per-function breakdown
is in `NEXT.md` for the next iteration; the JSON has exact file/line/label
per site.

**Step 2 — picked ONE site to actually fix this session** rather than
patch all 143 blind (no time to hand-verify bail semantics for 43
functions in one sitting, and a wrong bail target risks a worse bug than
the crash it's meant to prevent). Picked `selectPostCrawlCraft`
(`funcs_30.c`, 3 of the 143 candidates) because its name matches the
"SELECT-CRAFT" transition this project has instrumented and soaked
against for 30+ sessions. A full end-to-end read of the function (it's a
single ~800-line body, no other `RECOMP_FUNC` boundary inside — same
"decompiler never split it" pattern as `heapWalker`) found:
- Site 1 (`0x800CBBD8`, register `r16`/`$s0`): a "free every node in a
  list" loop — frees an `0x5C` sub-object then the node itself, walking
  via the node's own next-pointer field. **This is the one fixed this
  session.**
- Sites 2/3 (`0x800CBDA8`/`0x800CBDE4`): two near-identical inlined
  list-insert helpers appended to the tail of a list — NOT fixed this
  session, flagged in `NEXT.md` for a future iteration with their own
  trace.

**Important correction to the mechanical grep's own signature**: reading
site 1's loop body found the vulnerable pointer is dereferenced through
**two different registers** on loop entry — `ctx->r4 = MEM_W(ctx->r17,
0X5C)` immediately followed by the self-referential `ctx->r16 =
MEM_W(ctx->r16, 0X0)` — because `r17` and `r16` hold the same
(potentially corrupted) node address at loop entry (`ctx->r17 =
ADD32(ctx->r16, 0)` on every back-edge). A guard placed only before the
self-referential line, matching every prior guard's literal pattern,
would still leave the FIRST dereference (`ctx->r17`) exposed and
reachable — the crash could still happen one line earlier. The guard
added here sits immediately after the loop label, before either
dereference, checking `ctx->r16` (the value both registers share at that
point) against the standard KSEG0 bounds
(`0x80000000`-`0x80800000`, `hi==0xFFFFFFFF`). Bail target: `ctx->r2 =
S32(0X800D << 16); goto L_800CBC04;` — verified by reading forward from
`L_800CBC04` that `r2` there is an independent fixed constant
(`0x800D0000`, used only for one further `rs_free()` at a hardcoded
offset, never derived from `r16`/`r17`), and that the loop's own natural
exit path (`r16==0`) sets `r2` to this exact same constant before falling
into the same label — so the bail is indistinguishable from "list ended
here" to all downstream code, matching this codebase's established
"give up gracefully" bail contract. This asymmetry (mechanical grep
signature vs. the actual multi-register vulnerable window) is worth
carrying into the remaining 142 candidates — do not assume the
self-ref line alone is always the right/only guard point; read the whole
loop body first.

**Build**: mandatory delete-all-45-`funcs_*.c` → `make_elf.py` →
`regen_n64recomp.sh` → `fixup_game_funcs.py` → `cmake --build`. Patch
report audited: `funcs_30.c: selectPostCrawlCraft free-list-walk
loop-back guard (0x800CBBD8) patched x1` — exactly the expected
multiplicity, no duplicate. `cmake --build` exit 0. Binary verified fresh
(`strings build/RogueSquadron64Recomp | grep selectpostcrawl-guard` hits
exactly once, binary mtime matches the build).

**Soak** (`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/run_selectpostcrawlguard1.sh`,
tag `selectpostcrawlguard1`, all `campose11`-baseline guards armed plus
the new `ROGUESQ_LOG_SELECTPOSTCRAWL_GUARD=1`, `HOLD_S=150`): crossed the

## Session 250 (2026-07-28)

**Continued the s249 static sweep: guarded `selectPostCrawlCraft`'s other
2 candidate sites (`funcs_30.c`, 0x800CBDA8 and 0x800CBDE4 — the "two
near-identical inlined list-insert helpers" s249 flagged but didn't
trace). Build clean, no regression. 2 soak attempts: 1st pre-empted
pre-title-screen by an already-catalogued unrelated crash class (0/0
positive controls, uninformative); 2nd survived the full run (`CRASH: 0`)
but got zero positive-control fires of any kind — an honest single-sample
null with weak evidentiary value, not a confirmed clean pass. 140
candidate sites remain project-wide.**

**Full-loop-body read (mandatory per s249's own finding) of both sites.**
Both are byte-identical in shape: a doubly-linked-list "insert at tail"
helper, list head read from an untrusted struct field
(`MEM_W(ctx->r4, 0X20)` for helper A / `MEM_W(ctx->r4, 0X10)` for helper
B), walked to find the tail via a loop at `L_800CBDA8` / `L_800CBDE4`:

```
L_800CBDA8:
    ctx->r3 = MEM_W(ctx->r3, 0X0);   // flagged self-ref line (walk)
    ctx->r2 = MEM_W(ctx->r3, 0X0);   // peek-load of the BRAND NEW r3
    if (ctx->r2 != 0) goto L_800CBDA8;
```

This is a DIFFERENT shape from `selectPostCrawlCraft`'s own s249 guard
(two *different* aliased registers derived from the same pointer). Here
it's the *same* register (`r3`) dereferenced twice back-to-back: line 1
reads the incoming (possibly-corrupt, carried from the previous
iteration's own unvalidated walk) `r3`; line 2 immediately re-reads the
value line 1 just produced, itself unvalidated. This matches
`renderUnlitMeshFaces`'s s219 GUARD/GUARD3 combo shape (self-ref walk +
peek-load of the freshly-walked pointer), not `selectPostCrawlCraft`'s
own template — a guard only before line 1 would still leave line 2's
peek exposed to whatever garbage line 1 just read. So each site got TWO
guards this session (GUARD1 before the walk, GUARD2 between the walk and
the peek), both using the established `0x80000000..0x80800000` lo-half /
`0xFFFFFFFF` hi-half RDRAM-pointer sentinel check.

**Bail target: plain `return;`**, not a goto to a shared exit label like
s249's own guard used. Verified by reading forward: both sites' natural
loop-exit path writes `MEM_W(0X0, ctx->r3) = ctx->r5` (append into the
old tail's next field) then `MEM_W(0X4, ctx->r5) = ctx->r3` (new node's
prev = old tail) before returning — both use the untrusted `r3` as an
address or a stored value, so bailing into that path would just move the
wild dereference/store rather than avoid it. These are void-returning
internal helpers reached via `jal` (no `RECOMP_FUNC` boundary separates
them from `selectPostCrawlCraft` — they're folded into the same block by
the recomp naming heuristic) with no caller-visible error-code contract,
so silently abandoning the insert on a corrupt list is the simplest bail
this shape supports.

**Self-inflicted process note, worth remembering**: re-ran
`fixup_game_funcs.py` multiple times against the same already-patched
`funcs_*.c` output while auditing its report (`grep`-filtering the same
invocation repeatedly instead of saving one run's output to a file).
Most patches in this script are naturally idempotent (guard patches key
off an unguarded code *shape* that stops matching once patched), but at
least one older patch (`s139`'s `rs_malloc` entry-capture — matches a
literal function-prologue anchor that its own insertion doesn't consume)
is **not** idempotent and silently stacked duplicate declarations
(`redefinition of 's_rsmalloc_req_size'` etc.), breaking the build with
unrelated errors in `funcs_0.c`. Fixed by a fully clean re-regen (delete
all 45 `funcs_*.c` → `N64Recomp` → `fixup_game_funcs.py` **exactly
once**, output redirected to a file for later inspection rather than
re-invoked per question) and confirmed via `grep -c` on the resulting
file, not by re-running the script again. **Lesson for future sessions:
never invoke `fixup_game_funcs.py` more than once per regen cycle** —
save its report to a file and grep the file, not the live invocation.

**Build**: clean single-pass regen (see above). Patch report audited
(saved to `scratch/agent/s250_fixup_report.txt`): `funcs_30.c:

**Work unit**: s258 left a clear lead — `evalCubicSplineAtTime` (reached via

`buildPositionAndCallTransformHelper`) had an unguarded pointer feeding a
Bus error. Read all 3 functions in full (`funcs_4.c:25612-26093`,
`funcs_15.c:4019-4930`, `funcs_15.c:5758-5799`). `evalCubicSplineAtTime`

(`0x80018FF0`) as the base of the keyframe binary-search loop's first
read — identical "load struct field, deref immediately, no range check"
shape as every other guard in this project (`RENDERUNLIT_GUARD` is the
canonical example). Per NEXT.md's explicit instruction ("guard the
earliest unvalidated load found"), guarded this one, not the later
`ctx->r8`-based reads at `0x800190CC`+.

**Guard mechanics**: unlike `RENDERUNLIT_GUARD` (which reuses an existing
mid-function "list empty" label), `evalCubicSplineAtTime` has no partial-
skip path — the entire rest of the function (search loop, float
interpolation math, AND the r8-based reads) transitively depends on this
one struct. So a dedicated epilogue label (`L_evalspline_guard_exit`) was
inserted immediately before the function's real restore-and-return
sequence (guest `0x80019188`), and the guard `goto`s there directly. This
is ABI-safe because the prologue (`0x80018F9C`-`0x80018FB8`) already saves
`$s0`/`$s1`/`$f20`/`$f22`/`$f24`/`$f26`/`$f28`/`$f30` to their stack slots
strictly BEFORE this guard's anchor point (right after the r16 load) — so
every value the epilogue restores is already correct on the stack, same
ABI-safety reasoning s109 used for `L_dlentry_guard_exit`. New env var:
`ROGUESQ_LOG_EVALSPLINE_GUARD`. Output (`*a2`, the 3 interpolated floats)
is left as whatever the caller already had on a guard fire — leaving
stale data beats a crash, same trade-off every prior guard in this
codebase makes.

`regen_n64recomp.sh` → `fixup_game_funcs.py` exactly once — confirmed both

## Session 260 (2026-07-29) — closed s259's `setLookupEntryField5ByKey` lead, but it took two guards, not one: the caller-argument guard was a red herring, the real bug was a 2nd-level pointer loaded inside the callee's own search loop. **Work unit**: s259 left a precise lead — `activateAnimationKeyframe`'s
call to `setLookupEntryField5ByKey` (funcs_14.c:2116, the only one of 18
call sites in the file that falls inside `activateAnimationKeyframe`'s own
range 1629-2138) passed an argument (`ctx->r4`, loaded from `$s1+0xF4` at
guest `0x80061EF4`) that was checked ONLY against zero before being handed
to the callee, which dereferences it further with no range validation.

**First guard (`SETLOOKUP_ARG_GUARD`)**: widened the existing `if
(ctx->r4 == 0)` check to the standard KSEG0-range + hi-word idiom, but
implemented it by coercing an out-of-range value to 0 right before the
pre-existing check runs (rather than adding a parallel `goto`), so the
function's own `L_80061F18` bail path handles both cases identically — no
new label needed. New env var `ROGUESQ_LOG_SETLOOKUP_ARG_GUARD`.

accidentally run twice against the same regenerated source on the first
pass (a stray verification re-run), silently double-inserting the guard
block (2 copies of the same PATCH block back to back — harmless
functionally, since it's the same check twice, but violates "fixup runs

redirect `fixup_game_funcs.py`'s stdout to a file (`> scratch/agent/*.log`)
and grep it, rather than trusting a terminal `tail`, which can silently
truncate or hide a duplicate run.

**Soak 1 (`setlookupguard1`, 224MB `run.log`)**: `SETLOOKUP_ARG_GUARD` got
**0 fires**, but the run crashed with the **EXACT same signature** as
s259's crash — same call stack (`static_5_800AAD9C` →
`advancePlayerAnimationPhase` → `activateAnimationKeyframe` →
`setLookupEntryField5ByKey`), same `si_addr=0x3c04b1980`/
`x9=0x00000000c04b1980`, same ~VI-8192 crash mark. This is a genuine
discriminating result (not a null result — iron rule 1's positive-control
concern doesn't apply here because the ABSENCE of a fire combined with the
SAME crash recurring is itself informative): `ctx->r4` was demonstrably
clean on every call this run, including the crashing one, so the argument
was never the wild pointer.

**Re-read `setLookupEntryField5ByKey`'s body in full** (funcs_15.c:70-130)
to find the real bug: after the safe first deref (`ctx->r2 =
MEM_HU(ctx->r4, 0x4)`), the function's search loop (label `L_800646BC`)
reloads `ctx->r3 = MEM_W(ctx->r4, 0X0)` **on every iteration** — this is a
table-base pointer stored INSIDE the already-validated struct, a
genuinely distinct value from `ctx->r4` itself, not a re-read of the same
thing. The loop then computes `ctx->r3 = index*8 + ctx->r3` and
dereferences THAT (`ctx->r2 = MEM_W(ctx->r3, 0X0)`, guest `0x800646C8`)
with zero validation anywhere. `x9=0xc04b1980` matches this 2nd-level
pointer's shape exactly (a garbage value that's neither in the
`0x80000000`-`0x80800000` KSEG0 range nor zero) — the argument-level guard
could never have caught this because the argument itself genuinely was
fine.

**Second guard (`SETLOOKUP_TABLE_GUARD`)**: added at `0x800646BC`
(funcs_15.c), validating `ctx->r3` immediately after its load, bailing via
`ctx->r2 = 0; return;` if out of range — chosen to exactly match the
loop's own "not found" exit (`L_800646F0`, which also leaves `r2=0` and
returns) since no caller anywhere checks this function's return value,
only its side-effect byte write (`MEM_B(0X5, ctx->r3) = ctx->r6` at
`0x800646D8`) on the found-a-match path. New env var
`ROGUESQ_LOG_SETLOOKUP_TABLE_GUARD`.

## Session 264 (2026-07-29) — ran s263's prescribed 2nd `dequeueguard1` soak (iron rule 4); it crashed, not clean, and a direct ARM64 disassembly of the crash PC (first time this investigation has decoded the actual faulting instruction instead of reading symbol+offset) proves the crash is NOT inside `heapFreeListDequeue` at all — it's a different, previously-unseen unguarded store elsewhere in `submitSceneNodeRender`. **Crash detail**: `[CRASH][pc-symbol] pc=0x102fc4efc sym=submitSceneNodeRender+19268`, register dump `x0=x9=0x0000000300000000`, `x10=0x00000000f5f9f85c`, `si_addr=0x3f5f9f85c` (`si_addr == x9+x10` exactly). Backtrace: `submitSceneNodeRender` <- `processSceneNode` <- `traverseSceneGraphRecursive` <- `setupCameraMatrices` <- `static_5_800AAD9C` <- `static_5_800C6854` <- `menuOverlayInit` <- `mainGameLoop`.

**Disassembly (new methodology this session)**: wrote `scratch/agent/s264_symrange.py` (parses the Mach-O symbol table directly, no `nm`/`atos`/`otool` — none are on the Bash allowlist) to get `submitSceneNodeRender`'s real address range: `0x1006b43b8` to the next symbol `renderFlatMeshFaceGroup` at `0x1006bd650` (+37528 bytes). The crash offset (+19268) falls cleanly inside that range — **not** inside `heapFreeListDequeue`, which is a completely separate, distant symbol (`0x1004180e8`, ~29MB away). This is conclusive: whatever this run crashed on, it did not go through the guarded `heapFreeListDequeue` call sites at all. Then re-ran the already-existing `scratch/agent/s193_disasm.py` (a prior session's hand-rolled ARM64 load/store decoder, built specifically because `atos`/`otool`/`lldb` aren't on this sandbox's Bash allowlist) at `submitSceneNodeRender+19268`: the faulting instruction is `0xb82a6928`, which decodes to `STR w8, [x9, x10]` (register-offset store, opc=00, size=word) — a raw 32-bit store to host address `x9+x10`, i.e. exactly `si_addr`. `x9` is the RDRAM-base-ish register; `x10=0xf5f9f85c` is the wild operand actually driving the fault.

**The signature correction**: `PORTING-STATE` Session 219 (`:20646-20729`, `CURRENT-TRUTH` item -60, "Overturned conclusions") already proved, by reading `N64Recomp/include/recomp.h`'s real `MEM_W` macro, that `x0`/`x8`/`x9 = 0x0000000300000000` is this process's **constant, unchanging native RDRAM host base pointer** — it appears in literally every faulting `MEM_W`-style memory access in this binary "by construction, not corrupted data with a write site," and is therefore *not* a valid way to match one crash to another. s263's write-up (item -104) justified `DEQUEUE_GUARD` partly by "matching the crash's own repeated `x0=x9=0x0000000300000000` (guest 0x0) fault signature" — the exact fallacy s219 named and refuted 44 sessions earlier, apparently never checked against by s263 (`PORTING-STATE` is 44+ sessions and `CURRENT-TRUTH`'s "Overturned conclusions" section, while it does carry the s219 correction, is easy to miss when skimming ~455KB for a single work unit). This does **not** mean `heapFreeListDequeue`'s unguarded `a0` deref is not a real bug — source-reading it directly (s263) still stands as a legitimate, independently-justified finding, and `DEQUEUE_GUARD` costs nothing left armed — but it means the claim that this bug explains "the 18th crash class" specifically was never actually supported by the register evidence, only by a coincidence of the omnipresent base-pointer register matching across unrelated crashes.

Per s219's own distinguishing criterion (does the wild operand carry the KSEG0 tag shape `0x80xxxxxx`, indicating item -49's specific zero-extension bug, or not): `x10=0xf5f9f85c` has top nibble `0xf`, **not** `0x8` — so this is explicitly **not** a recurrence of item -49 (whose signature is the fixed literal `0x80630062`/`si_addr=0x380630062`), and not the `heapFreeListDequeue` bug either (wrong native address range). It is a **third, previously-uncatalogued site** in the broader "RDRAM-base + wild 32-bit garbage operand" store/load family already named in s257 ("10+ known call sites... not yet guarded") — structurally similar mechanism, independent occurrence.

**Discriminating outcome reached**: NEXT.md's own decision tree covered this exact case ("crashes at a genuinely different site/function: real forward progress... follow the new crash") — confirmed via disassembly, not just symbol-offset guessing, for the first time in this investigation. `DEQUEUE_GUARD`'s hypothesis (2 soaks, 0 fires both times, and now proven structurally unrelated to this run's actual crash) should be downgraded from "candidate fix for the 18th crash class" to "independently-justified hardening, unconnected to any crash observed so far" — do not spend a 3rd soak testing it as a fix; per budget rule 8 this hypothesis has had its 2 misses.

**New reusable methodology**: `scratch/agent/s193_disasm.py` (hand-rolled ARM64 LDR/STR/LDP/STP decoder, no `atos`/`otool`/`lldb` needed) plus the new `scratch/agent/s264_symrange.py` (Mach-O symbol table dump/range lookup) together let any future session precisely decode a crash's faulting instruction and confirm/refute which native function range it actually falls in, directly from `[CRASH][mcontext] pc=...` — this should be the FIRST step on every future crash triage, before re-reading source by eye or trusting the `pc-symbol` line's offset at face value.

Chose NOT to follow NEXT.md's literal step-by-step prescription (extend `s193_disasm.py` to decode branches, then eyeball-correlate branch/call density against `funcs_4.c`'s `jal`/branch comments to approximately narrow the crash to "a few hundred source lines"). That method is inherently fuzzy and was flagged by NEXT.md's own text as a stopgap next to a better option it named but deferred: "a cheap 'last executed guest PC' breadcrumb... would obsolete this manual correlation for every future crash — a generically high-value investment given 260+ sessions of exactly this localization bottleneck." Since every recompiled MIPS instruction in `funcs_4.c` already carries its own `// 0xGUEST_ADDR: mnemonic ...` comment (a 1:1 guest-address index, unlike the native ARM64 side which has no such index), stamping a global with that address at each instruction gives EXACT single-instruction localization for free, without any native-side correlation at all. This is the same goal NEXT.md's work unit specified, reached via the more reliable of its own two named methods.

**Implementation** (`g_rs64_last_guest_pc`, a `volatile uint32_t`):
- `recomp.h`: added `extern volatile uint32_t g_rs64_last_guest_pc;` next to the existing `extern int32_t* section_addresses;`.
- `src/main/main.cpp`: defined the global (`extern "C" volatile uint32_t g_rs64_last_guest_pc = 0;`, same pattern as the existing `g_recomp_rdram_for_wp_raw`/`rs64_get_vifs_crash_snapshot` cross-TU globals) and added `fprintf(stderr, "[CRASH][last-guest-pc] pc=0x%08x\n", g_rs64_last_guest_pc);` to the SIGSEGV/SIGBUS handler, right after the existing `[CRASH][pc-symbol]` dladdr line.
- `N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py`: new pass, scoped to `submitSceneNodeRender` only (not the whole binary — this is the one function 3+ consecutive sessions of crashes have converged on, and scoping keeps the diff and the added per-frame overhead small). Finds the function's body span via the same `func_re` used elsewhere in the script, then regex-inserts `g_rs64_last_guest_pc = 0xADDRu;` immediately after every `// 0xADDR: ...` comment line in that span, preserving whatever indentation the comment itself has (branch-delay-slot blocks are indented deeper than straight-line code). Runs LAST in the file so it also breadcrumbs the comment lines already-existing guard patches (DEQUEUE_GUARD etc.) leave behind — desired, since those are still real guest instructions.

**Non-obvious build gotcha found this session, worth remembering**: there are TWO `recomp.h` files in play. `~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp/include/recomp.h` is the standalone codegen tool's own header (only used by that tool internally); the actual game build's `RecompiledFuncs` target gets its headers from `RogueSquadron64Recomp/lib/N64ModernRuntime/N64Recomp/include/recomp.h` (a vendored copy inside the `N64ModernRuntime` submodule — see `CMakeLists.txt:92-97`'s `target_include_directories`, which lists the `lib/N64ModernRuntime/...` path, not the standalone tool's path, at all). Editing only the standalone copy (which is the natural first guess, since that's the tool whose `.toml`/binary you invoke for step 2 of the regen pipeline) produces a `cmake --build` failure ("use of undeclared identifier 'g_rs64_last_guest_pc'" x20, `funcs_4.c`) with no obvious link to the actual cause. Edited both copies for consistency; only the `lib/` copy is load-bearing for compilation. **Any future header-level addition needs to go in the `lib/N64ModernRuntime/N64Recomp/include/recomp.h` copy, not (only) the standalone tool's.**

**What ran**: per s283's plan, grepped every `-0X25A4` occurrence across `RecompiledFuncs/*.c`

(`funcs_19.c`) loads its `-0x25A4` offset off a base set via `lui $at, 0x8004`, a completely
different address than the hangar-list global's `lui $s1, 0x800D` — same offset, unrelated global
(a float constant table, not a pointer). The other 172 hits all confirmed `lui`-`0x800D`.

Per-function breakdown of the 172 confirmed hits: `hangarInitialize` (`funcs_27.c`) 103,
`static_5_800AB658` 32 (the pre-existing `G1`-`G32` whack-a-mole family), `static_5_800ADB70` 21,

`funcs_40.c` functions had NEVER been audited — delegated 3 parallel classification passes
(one per function) plus a scoping-only sample of `hangarInitialize` to background agents, each
reading the full function body and, for every hit, tracing whether the loaded pointer (or a value
derived from it) reaches a dereference with no preceding `0x80000000`-`0x80800000` range check.

Results: `static_5_800AAD9C` (2 hits) — both unguarded, identical shape (two near-duplicate scan
loops). `static_5_800AB1C8` (10 hits) — 4 already guarded (pre-existing sites 1/3/4/5), 1 safe
(loaded value only ever used as a call argument, never dereferenced in this function), 5 unguarded
(sites 6-10) — two of the five (6 and 10) are a "second-hop" variant: the EXISTING guard at that
site validates the *value loaded from* the dereference, not the pointer used to *reach* it, so the
first-level dereference itself was still exposed. `static_5_800ADB70` (21 hits) — all 21
unguarded, no bounds checks anywhere in the function; the 21 sites collapse into ~9 recurring
2-4-line shapes (load, add loop-index, dereference one or more fields), all converging on the same
single epilogue `L_800AE060`. Total: 28 genuinely unguarded sites across the 3 functions.

`hangarInitialize` (`funcs_27.c`, lines 119802-133178, 13,376 lines) was scoped ONLY, not touched
this session — a 22-site sample (spread start/middle/end) found 21 unguarded, 1 safe (the write

(returns) across its span plus 244 branch-target labels (not exit points); estimated 5-7 future
sessions to fully classify+guard at the same per-site rigor used here, given the sheer size.

(a small script walking backward from each dereference line to its immediately-preceding pointer
computation) and each anchor regex's uniqueness within `funcs_40.c` was verified via a dry-run
match count (all 28 matched exactly once) BEFORE splicing into `fixup_game_funcs.py` — avoiding
the risk of a shared/duplicated anchor text silently patching the wrong location. Landed 28 new
guards (`S284_AAD9C_1`/`_2`, `S284_AB1C8_6`/`_7`/`_8`/`_9`/`_10`, `S284_ADB70_1`-`_21`), same

**New finding, independent of the above**: validation soak2 (post-rebuild) crashed inside
`static_5_800A9270` at native `+1552` — confirmed genuinely within that symbol's own address range
via a Mach-O symtab walk (`start=0x100730c84`, `size=3352`, next symbol `static_5_800AAD9C`, not a
nearest-symbol misattribution). This function was declared "fully audited and validated
non-recurring as of s284" in `NEXT.md`'s do-not-touch list — but this is new, direct evidence
against that belief. Rather than rely on the crash alone, re-read the function's full source

was just reloaded from the `-0x25A4` global two instructions earlier (`0x800A92F0`) with NO guard

*after* this dereference and checks `r3` — the VALUE the dereference produced — not `r4`, the
pointer that was actually dereferenced to produce it. This is the third confirmed instance of the
"validate the loaded value, not the pointer that reached it" blind spot (after s282's `G32` and
s284's `SECONDHOP`), found this time by direct code reading rather than by chasing an exact
address-ratio match to the crash (soak3, run immediately after, did NOT reproduce this crash —
consistent with this whole bug family's established low, state-dependent firing rate; the fix
rests on the source-level proof, not on reproduction).

function's existing epilogue already used by all its other guards). Verified the anchor's
uniqueness in `funcs_40.c` before patching. **Process note (own mistake, corrected in-session)**:

Ran the dead-code-detection methodology (s286/287) on `playerSnowSpeederInit` (`funcs_27.c:144145-150543`,

audit target — there is nothing to guard here regardless of the function's live/dead status.

**Ran the classification anyway, since NEXT.md explicitly required verifying rather than assuming**:
the "may be a dead duplicate" hypothesis is **REFUTED**, not confirmed.
- Extracted every `// 0xADDR:` comment line (2552 of them) and checked address monotonicity across
  the whole function: **zero decreases, only expected delay-slot repeats** — the guest address
  stream is a single continuous non-decreasing run from `0x800AAAE0` to `0x800ACD98`, the shape of
  genuinely continuous translated code, not a live-prologue-then-spliced-in-duplicate-chunk pattern
  (which is what `hangarInitialize`'s dead chunks looked like — a big backward/discontinuous jump at
  the chunk boundary).
- Directly compared the instruction at each of the three addresses where `playerSnowSpeederInit`'s
  comment stream crosses a known-duplicated function's start address, against that function's own
  real first instruction:
  - `0x800AAD9C`: `playerSnowSpeederInit` has `ori $v0, $zero, 0xFFFF`; `static_5_800AAD9C`'s real
    first instruction is `addiu $sp, $sp, -0x30`. **Different.**
  - `0x800AB1C8`: `playerSnowSpeederInit` has `lw $a1, 0x0($s2)`, continuing a live instruction
    stream (previous line is `lui $a0, 0x8011` feeding an unrelated computation) — not a function
    prologue at all.
  - `0x800AB658`: `playerSnowSpeederInit` has `lwc1 $f0, 0x50($s0)`; `static_5_800AB658`'s real
    first instruction is `addiu $sp, $sp, -0x100`. **Different.**

A single diverging instruction at a byte-for-byte comparison anchor is sufficient to disprove
duplication (the same standard s286/287 used to *confirm* duplication elsewhere — exact match
required). All three anchors diverge. Combined with the whole-function address monotonicity, this
is decisive: `playerSnowSpeederInit` is real, continuously-translated, live code across its entire
span — it is NOT a dead duplicate of `static_5_800AAD9C`/`static_5_800AB1C8`/`static_5_800AB658`.

**What actually explains the s286/287 label-name overlap**: `playerSnowSpeederInit` occupies the
same *virtual* guest-address range as these three `funcs_40.c` functions (they're loaded via a
different overlay context), so its `L_<addr>:` labels share numeric names with theirs by pure
address coincidence — not because it contains a text/byte copy of their bodies. This is the same
overlay-address-reuse phenomenon behind `hangarInitialize`'s dead chunks, but manifesting
differently here: coincidental address/label overlap between two *live* functions from different
overlays, not a live function containing a dead copy of another's bytes.

`:2420-2428` — both structurally identical, a double-buffered read-ahead cache calling
`inflate_recomp` on alternating half-buffers, nothing unusual in either).

**Source-read finding (step 1, negative)**: `inflate_fast` is a faithful, complete instruction-for-
instruction port of the classic (K&M-era) zlib `inflate_fast` core decompression loop — literal
decode, length/distance Huffman table walks, and the final LZ77 copy loop, all present and matching
the expected control flow. Every `MEM_W`/`MEM_B`/`MEM_BU`/`MEM_H` access in the function is
translated straight from the original MIPS load/store with **no bounds or range check of any kind**
— but this is true of every `RECOMP_FUNC` in this codebase before a guard is added; nothing about
this function's *translation* stands out as buggy or different from ~15 other already-catalogued
crash sites in this same investigation (s130-s289). No recompiler-introduced defect found.

**Caller-argument finding (step 2)**: traced the 4 register arguments `inflate_fast` receives from
`inflate_blocks`'s call site (`funcs_7.c:12336-12347`): `bl`/`bd` (single bytes, bit-length values,
loaded from `$s1+0x10`/`+0x11`) are safe (used only to index a small fixed `inflate_mask[]` constant
table, never dereferenced as pointers); `tl`/`td` (the literal/length and distance Huffman decode
table base pointers, loaded from `$s1+0x14`/`+0x18`) are guest RDRAM pointers **used directly and
immediately as the dereferenced base for every symbol decoded in the hot loop, with no address-range
check on either at the call site or on entry to `inflate_fast`**. The other two structurally-trusted
pointers — `z` (z_streamp, loaded from the caller's own stack slot, `ctx->r15`/`$t7` internally) and
`s` (`inflate_blocks_statef*`, `ctx->r24`/`$t8` internally) — are the "self" state objects nearly
every zlib call trusts implicitly; less specific to this function, but equally unguarded.

**Reframing the s272 observation (the actual finding this session, corrects s272's framing)**: s272's
crash record reads `si_addr=0x380000003` (RDRAM base + guest `0x80000003`), and s272's own write-up
already flagged this as "3 bytes past the exact-`0x80000000` signature this whole investigation has
been tracking" — but that observation was never followed up because s272-s288 all believed
`inflate_fast` was a system-library call needing a different localization approach (s289 corrected
that belief). Working the arithmetic through this codebase's actual `MEM_B`/`MEM_BU` macros
(`N64Recomp/include/recomp.h:101-108`, which XOR the byte offset with 3 for MIPS big-endian byte
addressing *before* subtracting the `0x80000000` RDRAM base): a **register holding exactly 0** fed
into any `MEM_B`/`MEM_BU` access with an offset whose low 2 bits are 0 produces precisely
`rdram + 0x80000003` — an exact match for the observed fault, with no need to invoke a large garbaged
64-bit value or an exotic offset. **This means the s272 crash is not a novel zlib bug at all — it is
the same "guest struct field left at 0/uninitialized where a valid `~0x80000000`-range RDRAM pointer
was expected" signature this investigation has guarded roughly 15 times elsewhere since ~s130** (the
`-0x25A4` family, the `G1`-`G32` family, `tickWrappingTimerAccumulatorList`'s `0x80000004`,
`buildPositionAndCallTransformHelper`'s `0x80000010`, etc. — all small positive offsets from an exact
`0x80000000` base). The most likely candidates for the zero-valued register, per the caller-argument
trace above, are `tl`/`td` (if `huft_build` failed to populate the caller's Huffman-table fields before
this call) or one of the several `MEM_BU(reg, ...)` accesses inside the copy loop where `reg` is `p`
(input pointer, `ctx->r12`) or `q` (output pointer, `ctx->r11`) — but this is not yet confirmed,
only newly plausible; the existing evidence (a single, years-old crash record with a stale
`last-guest-pc`) cannot distinguish between these candidates.

tickTextureMaterialExpiry-guard` (s295-297 all ran it). `scratch/agent/SOAK-RESULTS.md` did not exist
this session (no queued soaks ran between s297 and this iteration, so no new `BREADCRUMB12`

maintenance not triggered and no `BREADCRUMB12` recurrence to react to, this session started the M5
design doc — `docs/M5-AUDIO-PLAN.md` did not exist yet, despite being deferred across s292-s297.

Delegated the survey to 3 parallel read-only agents (no session budget spent reading whole files
directly): (1) grepped `N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py` + `rogue_squadron.toml` + this repo's
`ROGUESQ_*` audio env vars; (2) grepped `lib/N64ModernRuntime` for RSP task dispatch, DMEM
serialization, and SDL audio wiring; (3) grepped `PORTING-STATE.md`/`PROJECT-OVERVIEW.md` for the
documented audio-adjacent crash history. Synthesized into `docs/M5-AUDIO-PLAN.md`.

**Key findings that correct the goal-stack's framing** (full detail and citations in the new doc):
1. The stub is a **single function-pointer swap** — `musyx_stub()` registered for `M_AUDTASK` in
   `src/main/main.cpp`'s `get_rsp_microcode()` dispatch switch (`main.cpp:594-595`), returning
   `RspExitReason::Broke` with zero ucode instructions executed. `factor5_ucode_b` (the recompiled
   MusyX ucode) is compiled and linked but never dispatched — dead code, not broken code. Everything
   else audio-related in `fixup_game_funcs.py` (the gate-byte force-zero, 8 div-by-zero traps, ~15
   diagnostic loggers, the s147 race fix) is either downstream of this one stub or, in the s147 case,
   independent of it entirely.
2. The `dmem[]`-sharing question the M5 goal-stack entry posed as an open design question is **already
   answered** by the s5 `g_lle_task_mutex`/`rs64_dmem_lock` mechanism — gfx and audio RSP execution
   already fully serialize through one recursive mutex around the one shared `dmem[0x1000]`. No new
   synchronization design is needed; only validation that it holds under real audio traffic.
3. The host audio bridge (`ultramodern::audio_callbacks_t`, `SDL_OpenAudioDevice`/`SDL_QueueAudio` in
   `main.cpp:622-638`, guest-facing `osAi*` functions in `librecomp/src/ai.cpp`) is **already fully
   implemented and functional** — confirmed, not assumed. De-stubbing needs zero host-audio-side work.
4. The crash-history survey found the goal-stack's rationale ("several recurring crash families are
   plausibly artifacts of the audio-disabled degenerate paths") is weaker than stated: of 4 documented
   audio-adjacent crash families, only 1 (the s1 boot-scheduler wedge) has audio-stub-as-root-cause
   **confirmed** by the docs' own text — and that one was fixed by disabling audio *harder* (the
   gate-byte patch), meaning de-stubbing directly re-exposes a previously-fatal hang unless the ucode
   now genuinely completes tasks. 2 of 4 (`waitForAnyAudioSlot` SIGSEGV, the post-cutscene stall
   hypothesis) are plausible-but-never-confirmed. 1 of 4 (the `voice+0x34` DMA race, s147) is confirmed
   **unrelated** to the disable state.
5. Separately flagged: `waitForAnyAudioSlot` (`fixup_game_funcs.py:2054-2119`) is a tight spin loop
   with no timeout, currently benign only because the stub resolves it instantly — real audio timing
   makes a genuine hang here more likely, worth a defensive bounded-timeout guard before real audio
   traffic flows.

**Plan landed in the doc**: a 6-step incremental sequence, each its own validation soak — (1) free
source-read determining whether the guest ever submits a real `M_AUDTASK` while the gate byte reads 0
(no code/soak); (2) swap the dispatch pointer only, gate still forced off (isolates "does the
recompiled ucode itself run without crashing" from the gate question); (3) land the
`waitForAnyAudioSlot` timeout guard as risk reduction; (4) reverse the 3 gate-byte sites one at a
time, watching specifically for crash family #1's exact historical signature recurring; (5) once
stable, the actual test of the goal-stack's rationale — soak-compare crash families #3/#4's rates
against their documented baselines, using the already-built diagnostic env vars for a same-run
positive control; (6) validate real (non-silent, non-garbage) PCM reaches SDL, not just that hangs
stopped.

**Rules out**: nothing new — this is a design/survey session, not an experiment. **Shows**: the M5
de-stubbing surface is much narrower (one dispatch-table entry) and the crash-family payoff case
weaker/more mixed than the goal-stack's phrasing implied — both corrections are now recorded so the
next session executes step 1 with accurate expectations rather than re-deriving them.

`docs/M5-AUDIO-PLAN.md`: new file (design doc, ~490 lines). No `lib/` changes this session — pure
survey + doc.

## Session 300 (2026-08-04) — executes M5-AUDIO-PLAN.md steps 1-2: resolves the gate/task-submission question and lands the recompiled MusyX ucode behind a validated, default-off env toggle

`docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md` measured 47,574 bytes at session start, under the 60,000-byte Step-0
maintenance trigger — proceeded straight to the top-priority work unit (M5, priority 2 per the USER
DIRECTIVE), continuing the thread `scratch/agent/NEXT.md` left as step 1 of the s298 plan.

### Step 1 — source-read (free, no code/soak)

Traced the audio-enable gate byte (`0x800A0F50`) forward through its 2 relevant readers in
`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/`:

- `tickMusyXIfActive` (`funcs_23.c:6785`, called from ~15 gameplay sites across
  `funcs_15/28/29/30/40/41/42/43.c`): a single `beq $v0,$zero,L_8008DA3C` at the top fully
  short-circuits the function when the gate reads 0, skipping `factor5MutexAcquire`,
  `tickActiveSongs`, `tickAndReap3DAudioVoices`, `stopAllSynthVoices`, `factor5MutexRelease` entirely
  — this is where songs/voices would normally get registered.
- `musyxSynthFrame` (`funcs_24.c:3146`) — the **separate** per-VI-retrace tick (caller confirmed s101
  to be `viRetraceHandlerThread`, independent of `tickMusyXIfActive`) — reads the same gate byte 5
  times in its body but only ever uses it to skip narrow slices: `update3DAudioFrame` (1 check) and,
  inside the per-voice loop, `tickAllActiveSongs`/`tickAudioSequencerFrame` (a 2nd read of the same
  byte, re-checked once per voice). The voice-mixing call (`musyxMixActiveVoices`) and a DMA-batch
  call (`LOOKUP_FUNC(ctx->r3)`, confirmed by the s102 diagnostic comment at that exact site to be
  `submitDmaRequestBatch`) sit on the unconditional path after the gate checks.
- Corroborating structural evidence: crash family #1 (M5-AUDIO-PLAN.md §3) — the *original incomplete*
  stub caused a boot-time scheduler wedge (`waitForMusyXAudioTaskDone` spinning on a countdown only
  real ucode execution decrements). That hang could only happen if the RSP audio-task pipeline already
  ran every frame regardless of the gate; the existence of that historical crash family is itself
  independent proof `M_AUDTASK` submission isn't gate-suppressed.

**s173 contradiction also resolved**: item -19's `PORTING-STATE` Session 173 entry inferred the gate
byte was "nonzero mid-run" from a crash backtrace passing through `tickMusyXIfActive`'s body (only
reachable past the gate check). A full-tree grep of every store to offset `0xF50` off base `0x800A`
found exactly **one** site that ever writes something other than a hardcoded literal 0:
`initMusyXEngine` (`funcs_23.c:9537`, `sb $v0,...` where `$v0=1` on init success) — the exact site
`N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py:94-101`'s regex force-zeros. `setDisplayMode`, `reapplyDisplayMode`,
`shutdownMusyXEngine`, `musyxNoopStub` each contain their own native `sb $zero,0xF50($at)` (hardcoded
0, no patch needed). So under the patch nothing in the recompiled guest code can legitimately set that
byte nonzero — if s173's inference was accurate, the only remaining explanations are (a) the patch
wasn't applied in that build, or (b) a wild/corrupting write clobbered ordinary BSS at that address
(this project's dominant crash theme). Not investigated further — flagged in `docs/M5-AUDIO-PLAN.md`
§1 for whoever next works crash family #3.

**Conclusion**: `M_AUDTASK` submission is NOT suppressed by the gate. Step 2 is not a provable no-op
— it's a live first exercise of `factor5_ucode_b`.

### Step 2 — dispatch swap + validation soaks

Landed `factor5_ucode_b` behind a new env toggle rather than an unconditional swap (`src/main/main.cpp`
`get_rsp_microcode()`'s `M_AUDTASK` case, ~line 594): `ROGUESQ_AUDIO_UCODE` (any non-`0` value) selects
the recompiled ucode; unset/`0` keeps `musyx_stub`, so default behavior is unchanged pending a human
decision to flip it on. Also added an always-on `[audtask-dispatch]` counter (first 20 dispatches then
every 256th) as a ground-truth check independent of the higher-level audio instruments.

That counter turned out to be necessary, not just belt-and-suspenders: the first validation soak (86s
wall, `ROGUESQ_AUDIO_UCODE=1`, all ~15 audio diagnostic env vars armed per the plan) ran clean — title
reached 45.1s, full key/stick sequence, 60s hold, 0 `[CRASH]` — but `ROGUESQ_LOG_MUSYX_DMA_CALL` and
`ROGUESQ_LOG_VOICE_TRIGGER_CHAIN` both logged **zero** hits. Rather than read that as "the ucode path
wasn't exercised" (a false-null risk explicitly against Iron Rule 1), traced further: those instruments
sit on `submitDmaRequestBatch`, the **PI-DMA sample-streaming path** (gated on real song/voice state,
which never gets populated since `tickMusyXIfActive` is fully short-circuited) — a different mechanism
from RSP task submission entirely, a distinction step 1's source trace had conflated. Added the direct
`[audtask-dispatch]` counter, rebuilt, re-soaked:

- **Control** (`ROGUESQ_AUDIO_UCODE` unset, `HOLD_S=15`): `real_ucode=0` confirmed from `n=0` at
  process boot — settles that `M_AUDTASK` dispatch is unconditional and immediate, independent of any
  toggle. Died mid-hold to a **pre-existing, unrelated** crash: `reserveAndEmitDLEntry` +
  `submitSceneNodeRender` chain, `x0=0x0000000300000000` (the known constant RDRAM host-base pointer,
  see Overturned Conclusions s219) — a scene-graph-traversal crash, nothing to do with audio. Confirms
  the unmodified baseline has nonzero crash rate too; not caused by this session's change.
- **Treatment** (`ROGUESQ_AUDIO_UCODE=1`, `HOLD_S=15`): `real_ucode=1` confirmed firing continuously
  from `n=0`, dispatch count into the hundreds within the run. Clean through title (44.8s) → 3xStart →
  a → probe → 15s hold with stick pulses → grace: **0 `[CRASH]`**, `exit=2: 0`, `UnhandledJump: 0`,
  `missing-func: 0`.

**Net across both treatment soaks**: ~1,500+ combined `M_AUDTASK`→`factor5_ucode_b` dispatches, 0
crashes, 0 hangs, title screen reached within the historical 45s baseline both times. `factor5_ucode_b`
itself is not observably broken under real dispatch load through boot/title/menu. This is 2 clean
runs, not the "multiple soaks, rate comparison" bar the plan's step 5 sets for crash-family questions
— sufficient for step 2's narrower "does the ucode itself crash/hang" check only.

**Rules out**: step 2 causing an immediate crash or pre-title hang (2/2 clean). **Shows**: the gate
byte's effect is narrower than either the goal-stack's framing or a naive reading of step 1's own
instrument choices suggested — it gates *guest-side bookkeeping* (song/voice registration), not RSP
task submission, which the SDK-level scheduler runs unconditionally every frame regardless of audio
content. **Method-trap generalization for `docs/PROJECT-OVERVIEW.md` §4.1** (instruments-that-lie):
an env-gated diagnostic firing 0 times is not evidence the code path was unreached until a
mechanism-independent counter confirms it — `musyx-dma-call`/`voice-trigger-chain` measured a
downstream, data-gated consequence, not the RSP-level fact being tested.

No `lib/` changes this session (`src/main/main.cpp` is this repo's own tree, not a submodule) — no
`submodule-patches/export.sh` needed.

## Session 301 (2026-08-04) — executes M5-AUDIO-PLAN.md step 3: lands and validates the `waitForAnyAudioSlot` bounded-timeout guard

Per the USER DIRECTIVE priority order (item -162's step 3): `waitForAnyAudioSlot`
(`N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_15.c:7217`) is a tight, uncapped spin —
`while (!anyAudioSlotActive()) { tickMusyXIfActive(); }` — currently benign because the stub's empty
voice state converges fast, but `ROGUESQ_AUDIO_UCODE=1` (s300) makes a genuine hang here newly
plausible with real dispatch timing, and step 4 (gate reversal, next session) makes it more so — a
pre-existing landmine independent of de-stubbing, not a hypothetical.

### The patch

Added a new guard block in `N64Recomp/fixup_game_funcs.py` (~line 2119, between the existing
loop-heartbeat and exit diagnostics from s163) that rewrites the loop's exit branch
(`0x800668CC: beq $v0, $zero, L_800668C0`): once the existing `g_audio_drain_iters` counter (already
incremented every iteration by the s163 heartbeat patch immediately above this branch) reaches a cap
(default 500,000, overridable via `ROGUESQ_WAITFORSLOT_GUARD_CAP`), the patch skips the
`goto L_800668C0` and falls through instead — forcing the same path as `ctx->r2 != 0` ("a slot is
active"), breaking the spin. Safe by construction: the very next *original* instruction after the
whole if/else (0x800668D0's `lui`, outside the patch's regex match) unconditionally reassigns `ctx->r2`
on every path regardless of which branch fires, so the guard's own effect on `ctx->r2` is moot — it
only changes whether the loop takes one more lap. Every fire is logged distinctly via the new
`ROGUESQ_LOG_WAITFORSLOT_GUARD` env var (fire count + iteration count + cap, matching the project's
"never silently indistinguishable from a normal exit" convention) so a fire can never be mistaken for
ordinary convergence.

Regenerated via `N64Recomp/build/N64Recomp rogue_squadron.toml` then `python3 fixup_game_funcs.py` —
all 4 `waitForAnyAudioSlot` patches (entry/heartbeat/**new guard**/exit) applied cleanly, `x1` each, no
collisions. Built clean (`cmake --build build -j8`, exit 0). No `lib/` changes this session (the edit
is in the `N64Recomp` tool checkout, which is not a submodule of this repo — it isn't git-tracked at
all in that checkout, per `git status` there; the durable record is this file plus the physical patch
on disk, same pattern the tool checkout has followed since session 1) — no `submodule-patches/
export.sh` needed.

### Validation: 3 soaks, `run_waitforslotguard1.sh` (new script,
`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/run_waitforslotguard1.sh`) — same env-var block as the established
`run_dequeuearg1.sh` reference recipe, plus `ROGUESQ_AUDIO_UCODE=1` (step 2's toggle, so the guard is
exercised under real ucode dispatch timing per the plan) and `ROGUESQ_LOG_WAITFORSLOT_GUARD=1`

- **Soak 1**: died at hold-iter ~0 (pre-scene, before VI width 1024) to `[CRASH] signal 11` inside
  `waitForAnyAudioSlot` (`+244`), called from `menuOverlayInit`. This is the exact, already-documented
  crash family #3 (`M5-AUDIO-PLAN.md` §3: "`waitForAnyAudioSlot` pre-title SIGSEGV (23rd crash class)",
  ~12-21% of historical pre-scene soak deaths). Confirms it's the *known* class, not a new one: **zero**
  `[audio-drain-enter]`/heartbeat/guard-fire lines appear anywhere in the run despite the crash PC
  resolving inside this function's compiled byte range — meaning execution never went through the
  function's actual entry point (which unconditionally logs on every real call) at all. Consistent with
  the crash being a corrupted/indirect jump landing mid-function rather than a legitimate call — the
  same "wild write" signature that dominates this project's crash taxonomy, not a symptom of this
  session's guard (which sits later in the function and never got a chance to execute).
- **Soak 2**: reached VI 1024 (45.3s), full key/stick sequence, SELECT YOUR CRAFT, entered the 240s
  hold window — 3 clean, legitimate `waitForAnyAudioSlot` calls logged first
  (`[audio-drain-enter] call=0/1/2`, `iters_this_call=1` each — confirms the loop's real steady-state
  convergence is ~1 iteration under the stub, nowhere near the 500,000 cap) — then died 5s into the
  hold to `[CRASH] signal 10 (Bus error)` in `emitAllocatedDLCommand`/`submitSceneNodeRender`,
  `x0=0x0000000300000000`. This is the *exact same* pre-existing, already-catalogued RDRAM-host-base
  signature s300's own control soak hit (Session 300, item -15 class #18/#14 lineage) — unrelated to
  audio entirely, a scene-graph-traversal crash. Guard fire count: 0.
- **Soak 3**: reached VI 1024, full key sequence, into the hold window with 3 more clean
  `[audio-drain-enter]` calls, 0 guard fires, 0 crashes — manually SIGKILLed after ~2 minutes (session
  time budget) rather than let it run the full 240s hold, since soaks 1-2 already gave the
  discriminating data needed. `run.log`: 3.5M lines, no `[CRASH]`.

**Net across 3 soaks**: guard fire count **0/3** (same-run isn't applicable here since the guard never
had a code path to prove-fire against in these soaks, but the *lack* of a fire across every legitimate
call observed — 3+1+3 = 7 real `waitForAnyAudioSlot` calls total, each converging in exactly 1
iteration — is consistent with the plan's own expectation that the stub's empty voice state converges
near-instantly, nowhere close to the 500,000 cap). Both crashes seen (2/3 soaks) are independently
identified as pre-existing, already-documented, unrelated crash classes — not new regressions from this
guard. Crash family #3 itself fired in 1/3 soaks here (33%), within/near its documented ~12-21%
historical range given the small n=3 sample (not a tight statistical match, noted honestly, but not
a rate increase either — no baseline-comparison claim is being made from n=3).

**Rules out**: the guard itself introducing a new crash or hang (0 evidence of that across 3 runs, 2 of
which hit *unrelated* pre-existing crashes that occurred entirely outside/before the guard's own code
path could execute). **Shows**: the guard is inert exactly as designed — discriminating outcome #1 from

## Session 304 (2026-08-04) — source-read of `setDisplayMode` vs `initMusyXEngine`'s gate-byte writes: refutes "wrong value"/naive call-frequency, surfaces a new toggle structure and an unconfirmed "`initMusyXEngine` may be dead code" side-finding

**Work unit**: per s303's explicit next-step ("do not retry `setDisplayMode`'s site blind... a FREE
source-read, no build/soak"), read `N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_23.c` around all three gate-byte
write sites (`initMusyXEngine` `0x8008E9F8`, `setDisplayMode` `0x8008EB40`, `reapplyDisplayMode`
`0x8008EC88`) and traced backward to where each site's `$v0` is computed, plus grepped for callers.

**Branch 1 (wrong value written) — REFUTED.** `setDisplayMode`'s write source is
`0x8008EB38: addiu $v0, $zero, 0x1` — a simple immediate constant, textually identical in shape to
`initMusyXEngine`'s already-reversed site (also `addiu $v0, $zero, 0x1`). `reapplyDisplayMode`'s site
is the same pattern. No computed/branch-dependent value anywhere at any of the three write sites — all
three write the literal constant `1`.

**Branch 2 (call-frequency) — refuted for `setDisplayMode` specifically.** Grepped every
`RecompiledFuncs/*.c` file for a direct `jal` to `setDisplayMode`'s entry (`0x8008EA14`): exactly one
hit, in `mainBootstrapWorker` (`funcs_0.c:486`), no loop or retry wrapping it — a straight-line
boot-once call, same shape as `initMusyXEngine`. (`reapplyDisplayMode`'s entry `0x8008EB5C` **is**
called every video frame, from `runVideoFrameTick` — a real call-frequency difference — but that's a
different, still-untouched site and doesn't explain s303's `setDisplayMode`-specific hang.)

**New structural fact, not anticipated by either branch**: `setDisplayMode` (and `reapplyDisplayMode`)
each contain their *own* entry-time unconditional zero-write to the same gate byte
(`0x8008EA34: sb $zero, 0xF50($at)`, executed before anything else in the function), sandwiching the
full MusyX-reset call sequence — `resetSongSubsystemCounter` → `initSongSequencerPools` →
`resetMusyXEngineState` → `clearStreamedVoiceFlags` → `reset3DAudioLists`, gated by an earlier call to
`initAudioSubsystem` (an early-return branch skips the whole reset-and-reenable tail if
`initAudioSubsystem` fails) — between a disable and the tail re-enable. This is a genuine 0→1 toggle
across a single call. `initMusyXEngine`'s site has no entry zero at all — it runs the same reset
sequence once and unconditionally sets the gate to 1 at the very end, no toggle.

**Leading revised hypothesis, cross-referencing s300 (item -162)**: the gate byte's only known consumer
is `musyxSynthFrame`'s per-VI-retrace tick, which — when gate=1 — additionally calls 3 functions that
are fully skipped when gate=0: `update3DAudioFrame`, `tickAllActiveSongs`, `tickAudioSequencerFrame`.
These have never executed in any soak validated to date. s303's writeup dismissed "first-ever execution
of these 3 functions" as sufficient explanation, reasoning gate=1 was "already exercised for ~75s in
s302's soaks... without incident" via `initMusyXEngine`'s reversal. **This session's grep puts that
premise in question**: an exhaustive text search of every `RecompiledFuncs/*.c` file for (a) a direct
`jal` to `initMusyXEngine`'s address (`0x8008E940`) and (b) any `lui`/`addiu` hi/lo pair constructing
that address as an absolute pointer (the pattern this codebase's own `LOOKUP_FUNC` indirect-dispatch
idiom would use) found **zero references anywhere outside `initMusyXEngine`'s own function body**. A
supplementary raw-byte scan of the 16 MB ROM (`rs64.n64.us.1.0.z64`) for the literal 4-byte address,
looking for a function-pointer-table entry, also found zero hits — but this check **failed its own
negative control**: `setDisplayMode`, confirmed reachable via `jal` (see above), *also* scores 0
raw-byte ROM hits, because MIPS `jal` encodes a shifted 26-bit target field, not an absolute 32-bit
address, so a raw-byte scan cannot distinguish "unreferenced" from "reached only via `jal`, like every
other function in this file." That check is discarded, not counted as evidence, per the "positive
control before trusting a null" rule.

**What survives**: single-source (text-grep only) evidence that `initMusyXEngine` may never be called
by anything currently in `RecompiledFuncs/`. Not yet promoted to a conclusion — doesn't rule out an ELF
relocation/overlay mechanism the grep wouldn't catch. If true, it would mean s302's "clean" 2-soak
validation never actually exercised gate=1 at all, `setDisplayMode`'s s303 reversal was the *first* real
gate=1 the recompiled game has ever hit, and "first-ever execution of the 3 previously-skipped
functions" becomes the leading (not ruled-out) explanation for the hang, rather than something specific
to `setDisplayMode`'s own write.

**Next work unit** (build+soak, next session): add a cheap entry counter/log to `initMusyXEngine`
(settles reachability — needs its own same-run positive control, e.g. a matching counter on a
known-always-called neighbor like `resetMusyXEngineState`, to rule out "logging itself is broken" as
the null explanation) batched with entry/exit tags on `update3DAudioFrame`/`tickAllActiveSongs`/
`tickAudioSequencerFrame` (ready for whichever branch the reachability result points to). Soak the
*current* baseline first (`initMusyXEngine` reversed per s302, `setDisplayMode`/`reapplyDisplayMode`
still force-zeroed — no site touched this session) before re-attempting `setDisplayMode`'s reversal.

No `lib/` changes this session (read-only against `N64Recomp/RecompiledFuncs/funcs_23.c` and
`funcs_0.c`, both regenerated files, no source edits). No build, no soak.

## Session 309 (2026-08-04) — M5 audio: source-read REFUTES s307's "audio-tick and RSP-task freezes are in lockstep" claim; the two are separate stalls, not one

Step 0 check: `wc -c docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md` = 46,006, under the 60,000-byte trigger — not a maintenance
session. Per NEXT.md, this session ran Step 1 of the trace-task-#40 work unit: a source-read of
`src/main/main.cpp` cross-referenced against s307's already-captured log
(`scratch/s73_post_a_scene/step307reach/run.log`), no new build or soak (per the work unit's own
"no build/soak yet" instruction).

**What the source read found.** `src/main/main.cpp:485`'s `[runner] task #%d …` print lives inside
`factor5_gfx_runner` (line 192), which `get_rsp_microcode` (line 581) returns **only** for
`M_GFXTASK`. `M_AUDTASK` dispatch is a completely separate branch of that same switch (line 594-626)
with its own counter, `[audtask-dispatch] n=%u …` (line 620) — a distinct code path that never touches
`factor5_gfx_runner` or its `[runner]` print. NEXT.md's and s307's framing — "the shared factor5_ucode
task runner that dispatches BOTH graphics DL tasks and audio ucode tasks through one path" — is **wrong
by source inspection**: there is no shared runner between the two task types; only the RSP-microcode
*dispatch table* is shared, and it branches immediately.

**What re-reading the log with that fact in hand found.** Cross-referencing line numbers, not just
task/tick counts: `[audtask-dispatch]`/`[reach-allsongs-*]`/`[reach-audioseq-*]` (the audio-tick chain)
permanently stop at `n=19` at **log line 3013**, which lands between graphics tasks #21 and #22 (`[runner]
task #22` is at line 3069). Graphics tasks then keep dispatching cleanly for **18 more tasks** (#22
through #39, ending line 4943) — roughly 1900 more log lines / a meaningfully later point in wall time.
In the window between the audio stop (line 3013) and the graphics stop (line 4943), the cooperative
scheduler is provably still alive and healthy: 1550 `[sched-queue]`/`[sched-check]`/`[sched-runnext]`
lines, cycling the **same 7 distinct thread pointers** that were cycling before the audio stall (verified
by diffing `popped_thr=`/`self_thr=` sets in the windows `[1857,3013)` vs `[3013,4943)` — identical set,
plus one incidental new thread). Only *after* task #39 (from line 4958 onward) does scheduler activity
stop completely — 0 further `[sched-*]` lines in the remaining 2467 log lines, a genuine full-scheduler
wedge, but a **separate, later** event from the audio stall, not the same moment.

**This refutes s307's core claim** ("task #39 is the last one ever dispatched, in lockstep with the
audio-tick freeze… both followed by pure scheduler churn with no new work") and the "shared upstream
resource… stops feeding both audio ticks and RSP tasks after a fixed count" hypothesis it produced. The
two freezes are sequential and mechanistically distinct: (A) an isolated audio-tick-producer stall at
tick 19→20, happening while the rest of the scheduler runs normally for a further ~18 graphics-task
cycles: 18 real, non-trivial live thread-swap events, not an idle gap, so this isn't a
timing-window artifact. (B) a full cooperative-scheduler wedge (all thread swapping stops) that happens
later, coincident with graphics task #39. Only (A) is directly relevant to M5 (it's the audio-tick loop
freezing); (B) may be an unrelated, more general bug — possibly the same class as the already-documented
"post-leave graphics-task-submission stall" (`docs/CURRENT-TRUTH.md`'s Current-truth timeline, ~90-115s
post-leave-SELECT-YOUR-CRAFT) but that is an untested hypothesis, not a finding — the post-leave stall
happens at a much later game phase under different conditions.

**One earlier false lead ruled out in the process**: an initial diff of `popped_thr=`/`self_thr=` thread
sets across the *entire* pre-3013 log vs the post-3013 log showed a thread (`0x30010d3d0`) present before
and absent after, which looked like a promising "the audio thread stopped being scheduled" signal (H1)
— but it last appears at line 174, hundreds of lines before the *first* RSP task even starts (line 775),
so it's an early-boot thread unrelated to the steady-state audio-tick loop, not evidence of anything.
Narrowing the comparison window to steady-state ticking (`[1857,3013)`) before comparing showed no thread
disappears at all — refuting H1 in its simple form (the audio-driving thread is not being dropped from
scheduling outright; it's plausibly still scheduled but silently not reaching the tick print, or the
print condition/gate itself changed). No same-run positive control existed for this specific
thread-identity claim either way — it needs a dedicated instrument (below), not more staring at existing
logs.

**Rules out**: the "shared task runner"/"lockstep" framing from s307 (source-level fact, not inference).
**Confirms**: s307's raw numbers (39 RSP tasks, audio ticks stuck at n=19, no crash, 600s) are all still
accurate as *measurements* — only the "these are the same event" interpretation was wrong.

`setDisplayMode`/`reapplyDisplayMode` still force-zero every call (baseline unchanged from s306/s308).

   decrement-then-compare-to-zero: `taken(skip) = (countdown_pre_decrement != 1)`. Since s311 already
   found `countdown` reads a constant `0` on every sample, this branch is **provably always "skip"**
   (0 != 1) — algebraically derivable from s311's own data without a new build. Confirmed at runtime
   this session anyway (see below) rather than trusted blind.
2. `[musyx-gate1]`, and the 2 other near-identical gate copies s107 found (funcs_24.c:3714, 3841), all
   read/write the SAME shared global pair (`-0x68EC` countdown / `-0x68E8` period) — a single shared
   resource across all 3 copies, not 3 independent counters as the "near-identical gate copies" framing
   might suggest.
3. **`update3DAudioFrame` (the 1st of the "3 gate-consumer functions") is NOT gated by this countdown
   maze at all.** It has its own, much simpler, independent gate near the top of `musyxSynthFrame`
   (`funcs_24.c:3242-3259`, guest `0x800912A8-0x800912BC`): read the raw byte at `0x800A0F50` (the
   SAME byte `setDisplayMode`/`reapplyDisplayMode`/`initMusyXEngine` force-zero) once, and call
   `update3DAudioFrame` unconditionally if it's nonzero — no countdown, no period, no other condition
   in between the read and the call (source-confirmed by direct reading of the generated C, not
   inferred). This makes `update3DAudioFrame`'s call frequency a **direct, single-variable proxy** for
   the raw gate byte's value across time, independent of the gate1/2/3 maze entirely.

carries real return-address information for *indirect* calls (function-pointer dispatch through a lookup
table), never for the plain-`jal`-translated calls all 3 known gates use. So `ra=0` at
`tickAudioSequencerFrame`'s entry is simply whatever stale value `ctx->r31` held from an earlier,

`funcs_24.c`) for both direct calls (`tickAudioSequencerFrame(rdram`) and any reference to its guest
address (`8008D960`, for an indirect/function-pointer dispatch pattern à la s310's `musyxSynthFrame`
finding). Result: **exactly the same 3 direct call sites system-wide, zero indirect/data-load references
anywhere.** This DEFINITIVELY REFUTES the "4th, unlocated call site" hypothesis carried forward from
s316 -- there is no other way into `tickAudioSequencerFrame` in the entire recompiled codebase, direct or

DIFFERENT source register from all 6 known gate writes (which all use `ctx->r2`), confirming this is a

it does not by itself explain gate1's countdown reading exactly 0 on all 40 samples in one run (that would
need a per-frame or per-call reset). Also noted `funcs_32.c:29181` computes an address using `-0X68EC`

**Rules learned (worth remembering for future indirect-call-hunting sessions):** `ctx->r31` in this
recompiler's codegen is NOT a general-purpose "log the caller" instrument -- it's only meaningful right

distinct sentinel write at each call site read back inside the callee, or (b) exhaustive textual/data-flow
search for the guest address, which is what actually discriminated the "4th call site" hypothesis here.

initializes to 0 at boot -- not an unconditional per-frame call. **Ruled out as a per-frame reset
mechanism.** `funcs_32.c:29181`'s `-0x68EC` reference turned out to be `lui $a0,0x800B; addiu
$a0,$a0,-0x68EC` -- a completely different base register computing an unrelated game-object pointer
argument for `dealDamagetoDatItem`, a coincidental hex-literal match, not a real reference to the audio
countdown at all. A full re-grep of every `0x68EC`/`0X68EC` occurrence in `RecompiledFuncs/*.c`,
filtered for the actual `lui $at,0x8015`/`-0x68EC($at)` addressing pattern the gates use, confirms

call;`). The diagnostic's `taken_skip` field, however, is computed from a SEPARATE, freshly-issued
`MEM_W(-0X68EC, 0X80150000)` re-read a few statements later -- NOT `ctx->r2`. gate1/gate2/gate3 all
read-modify-write this exact same shared word, and genuinely run under the coop scheduler's real
concurrency (confirmed multi-thread execution is a running theme across this whole M5 lineage, e.g.
s310's VI-retrace-callback finding). If another gate's write lands between the diagnostic's own read
and the real load that already happened, `taken_skip` can show a stale/wrong value that has nothing to
do with the actual branch outcome.

register value) as a new `reg=` field alongside the existing fresh re-read in all 3 gates

deterministic phase-timeout (exit 5, INCONCLUSIVE, VI stuck waiting for width 1024) -- the known,
accepted outcome for this reversed-site recipe, not a tooling failure; game process confirmed dead
before and after.

all 40 samples, exactly matching every prior session's reading. The new `reg=` field, however,
alternates `2,1,2,1,2,1,...` -- 19 of the 40 samples have `reg=1`, meaning the REAL branch
(`if (--reg != 0) skip; else call;`) took the **call** path on those 19 iterations. gate2 (only 4 of its

call. gate3 remains 0 samples reached (a reachability fact, unaffected by this bug, unchanged from

**Rule learned (general, worth remembering for future diagnostic design in this codebase):** when a
diagnostic needs to report "what branch will this code take," it must reuse the SAME register/value the
real branch logic already loaded, not issue a second independent read of the same memory location --
especially for any shared/global state touched from more than one call site under this project's
cooperative-threading model. A second read is not equivalent to the first even when they're only a few
C statements apart; anything else with write access can land between them. This is now a standing check
for reviewing any of this lineage's existing diagnostics that log shared (not call-local) state.

(tickAllActiveSongs) — 5 hits, all `lwc1 $fN, ±0x6D08($at/$r1)` float stack loads (base = stack pointer,

## Session 322 (2026-08-04) — M5 audio: gate3's containing reachability guard is REAL control flow, not an s318-class diagnostic bug — closes hypothesis (b), leaving only the untractable "fully dynamic indirect call" as the surviving 14-call-gap explanation; pivots the hypothesis-id to the fresher, unexplored 37-vs-40 gap

Continued `HYPOTHESIS-ID: m5-audio-destub-step4-setdisplaymode-hang`. Item -180 (s321) left one
cheap, read-only check outstanding: whether gate3's persistent "0/40 reached, containing code path never
entered" measurement is itself unreliable the way gate1/2/3's `taken_skip` field was until s318 found it
read a stale re-fetch of shared memory instead of the register (`ctx->r2`) the real branch actually uses.
Pure source-read against the already-current `RecompiledFuncs/funcs_24.c` (`~/Documents/Tools/N64Recomp`
checkout) — no build, no soak, no reversal.

**Method.** Read the full ~280-line span covering all three gates' setup, loop bodies, and every branch
target from `funcs_24.c:3519` (start of the enclosing loop nest) through `funcs_24.c:3927` (gate3's loop
continuation past its diagnostic block), tracing every `goto`/branch target by hand rather than just the
already-instrumented bodies s313-s321 had examined.

**Finding — the three gates are NOT three independent, symmetric checks; they form a cascade with
asymmetric bypass behavior:**

- **Gate1's entry guard** (`funcs_24.c:3524-3534`): `MEM_HU(-0x6678) < N` (N = a passed-in threshold,
  loaded into `s4`/`ctx->r20`). If false, jump directly to `L_800914E8` (gate2's setup) — normal
  cascade. If true, enter gate1's loop with `r19=0` (`s3`, a voice-index cursor shared by all three
  gates), `r16=MEM_HU(-0x6678)`, `r20=N` (unchanged for the rest of the function).
- **Gate1's loop, BOTH exit paths, go around gate2/gate3 entirely.** The outer per-iteration check
  (`L_80091444`, `funcs_24.c:3546-3560`: `r19 < MEM_HU(-0x68B2)`, a DIFFERENT address from the entry
  guard's) exits to `L_80091654` — the function's single shared FINAL label, past gate3's own loop — when
  false. The inner counter check (`after_11`, `funcs_24.c:3659-3668`: `r16 < r20(N)`) does the same.
  Every exit from gate1's loop, once entered, lands at the final label. **Structural consequence: any
  call where gate1's guard succeeds and its loop runs can never reach gate2 or gate3 in that same
  call, by direct jump — not by chance, by construction.**
- **Gate2's entry guard** (`L_800914E8`, `funcs_24.c:3677-3688`): rereads the SAME `-0x6678` address
  gate1's entry guard used, but against a fixed constant `0x10` instead of `N`. If false, converge at
  `L_800915A4` (gate3's setup region). If true, enter gate2's loop.
- **Gate2's loop, BOTH exit paths, flow onward toward gate3's setup** (`L_800915A0`/`L_800915A4`) —
  unlike gate1's, neither of gate2's exits (`L_80091504` top check on the same `-0x68B2` address vs.
  `r19`, or the inner `r16 < 0x10` check at `after_14`) targets the final label directly.
- **Gate3's setup** (`funcs_24.c:3821-3838`): reads `r20 & 0xFFFF` — i.e. `N`, the SAME register gate1's
  entry guard set up and NEVER rewritten since (confirmed: `grep -c "r20"` across the whole
  `funcs_24.c:3546`-`3822` span finds only 3 occurrences, all reads, zero writes). If `N==0`, skip
  gate3's loop entirely (final label). Otherwise enter gate3's loop, which has its own `r19 <
  MEM_HU(-0x68B2)` top check (same address/register gate1's inner check used, but `r19` was never reset
  since gate1's `r19=0` — it only carries the cumulative count of voices gate1+gate2's loops already
  processed).

**Verdict: no s318-class mismatch exists.** `ctx->r20` at gate3's guard is not a diagnostic proxy reading
stale shared memory — it *is* the literal register the real recompiled branch tests (this is generated
code executing the actual branch, not an instrument observing it from outside), and it is provably
unclobbered since gate1's setup. There is no register/memory divergence to find. Gate3's reachability is
governed by real game/voice-count state: **it is reachable ONLY when gate1's entry guard fails (so its
bypass-to-final-label never triggers) AND `N != 0` AND gate2's own `<0x10` guard succeeds AND the shared
voice cursor (`r19`, already advanced by up to 16 iterations from gate2's own loop) hasn't caught up to
`MEM_HU(-0x68B2)` by the time gate3's own top check runs.** That window is narrow but not empty — gate3's
observed 0/40-always across every soak since s313 is a real fact about the tested game state/scene, not a
measurement bug.

**This closes hypothesis (b) exactly as s321 closed hypothesis (a).** Both proposed explanations this
investigation could test via source-read for the 14-call gap (gate1+gate2's measured real-call rate,
23-24, vs. the tick-producer functions' own measured entry count, 37-38) are now exhausted. The only
surviving explanation — a fully dynamic indirect call resolved through a runtime-computed pointer chain,
among 28,388 `LOOKUP_FUNC(ctx->rN)` call sites — is explicitly not tractable by grep/read-only
methodology (per s321) and would need a different tool entirely (e.g. runtime call-site logging keyed on
the target function's address, not text search).

**Pivot.** Per NEXT.md's own pre-declared fallback and iron rule 8 (this closes the 16th consecutive
session on this exact hypothesis-id, all read/grep avenues now exhausted), this session identifies a
FRESHER, unexplored lead to pivot to instead of continuing to chase the untractable dynamic-call
explanation: item -174 (s315) already found and left open a DIFFERENT, smaller gap that this
investigation's -175..-180 branch never actually addressed — the 3 tick-producer functions
(`tickAllActiveSongs`/`tickAudioSequencerFrame`/`tickAllAudioChannels`) stop 3 calls short (37/37) of
the hard-freeze boundary shared by `update3DAudioFrame`, `M_AUDTASK` RSP-task submission (`[audtask-
dispatch]`, already widened and always-on in `src/main/main.cpp:581-636`, no `lib/` edit needed), and
the RSP task-runner's own last dispatch, all of which hit 40/40 together. That "37-vs-40" gap has had
ZERO dedicated investigation sessions (vs. the 14-call gap's 16) and is arguably closer to the actual
boot-hang mechanism, since 40 is exactly the point everything — including the RSP task runner — freezes.

## Session 323 (2026-08-04) — M5 audio de-stubbing: source-read closes the "internal early-return" branch of the tick37-vs-hardstop40 hypothesis, then a NEW runtime instrument (not text grep) finds a positive-controlled ZERO indirect calls to either tick-producer function

**Step 1 — source-read (NEXT.md steps 1-2), no build needed.** Read the full bodies of all 3
tick-producer functions: `tickAllAudioChannels` (`funcs_23.c:4061-6664`), `tickAudioSequencerFrame`

(`grep -c '^\s*return;'`) each has **exactly ONE `return;` statement**, at the very end, reached by every
internal branch via label fallthrough/goto (e.g. `tickAudioSequencerFrame`'s internal `beq $a0,$zero`
gate, taken or not, always converges at the shared `L_8008D9F0` label before the single return) —
independently re-confirming a claim `fixup_game_funcs.py`'s s306 comment already made but this session
verified fresh by direct grep rather than citation. Also confirmed the entry diagnostics (`[tick-audio-seq]`,
`[tick-all-audio-channels]`, `[reach-allsongs-entry]`) are inserted at the literal top of each function,
before ANY internal gate logic — unconditional on function entry. **Conclusion: no internal early-return
mechanism exists that could explain an entry/exit asymmetry, and — more importantly — since entry itself
is unconditional, the "37" stop is proven to be a fact about how many times the function is CALLED, not
something happening inside it.** This directly refutes NEXT.md's own working premise ("whatever stops the
tick-producers must be inside them or their direct callees, not further upstream") — that premise conflated
gate1's own reachability count (40/40, confirmed s320) with gate1 actually taking its "call" branch
(only ~19/40, per s318). The stop is upstream, in whatever mechanism drives calls to these functions — the
same, not-fully-identified mechanism the "14-call gap" investigation (items -180/-181) was chasing before
s322 called it exhausted by text tools.

**Step 2 — built a NEW runtime instrument instead of resuming the abandoned grep-only chase.** Found an
existing, precedented pattern for exactly this need: `rs64_log_dma_ring_caller` in
`lib/N64ModernRuntime/librecomp/src/overlays.cpp` (s101 precedent, closed lineage) hooks `get_function()` —
the ONE place every `LOOKUP_FUNC`/indirect call in the recompiled code resolves through — and fires a
native backtrace when the resolved address matches a specific target. Added `rs64_log_tickfunc_caller`
using the identical pattern, targeting `tickAllActiveSongs` (0x80096D08) and `tickAudioSequencerFrame`
(0x8008D960), gated behind a new `ROGUESQ_LOG_TICKFUNC_CALLER` env var. This is a genuinely different tool
from s317/s321's exhaustive text grep — it catches a fully dynamic indirect call at runtime, which no
static text search could ever find (item -180's explanation (a), left untested by text tools since it's
untestable by text tools).

the first soak (`setDisplayMode`'s site reversed a 14th time, narrowed regex to `C88`-only per the
established convention) found `[tickfunc-caller]`=0 hits — but ALSO `[dma-ring-caller]`=0 hits, meaning
the existing s101 positive control never fired either (the boot-hang phase this soak reaches, VI stuck at
320/rdpFs=39, plausibly never exercises `submitDmaRequestBatch`'s indirect call site, which lives in a
DMA-ring code path not reached before the freeze). A null with no live positive control in the same run is

to either tick-producer function — zero, not merely undetected.**
