## Session 632/633 — 2026-08-10 — first-ever fed fail136c discriminator: `reason=corrupt`, selected-pool E8 freelist walk breaks mid-scan (item -390/-391)

Consumed the two queued accumulation soaks from s631 (`s632_thr11d_rate_accum_a`,
`s633_thr11d_rate_accum_b`, mechanically identical to s631's recipe,
`HOLD_S=210`). `s632` had 1 attempt, `recov768=0` (silent) — no new data
point for the recovery-fired tally other than the denominator. `s633` scored
on its very first attempt: `recov768` fired, and — for the first time in this
campaign — **`thr11d_new=1` AND `ltexmg≥1` AND a scored `fail136c` all landed
in the same attempt.** Every prior `thr11d_new=1` sample (s629 att4) had been
killed by the `loadDatFile+692` background-noise crash before ever reaching
`ltexmg`; this is the first sample that survived long enough to actually
exercise the -389/-390 discriminator.

### The discriminator result: `reason=corrupt`, not a clean no-fit
`s633` `SCORE`: `thr11d_new=1 ltexmg=1 sec4_post=1 diag_fail136c=1 diag_ok136c=1
diag_reason=corrupt diag_maxfree=0x6A3E0 diag_maxfree_sel=0xD20 diag_nfree_sel=3
diag_need=0x1370 ship_store=2 ship_zero_post=2`. `maxfree_sel=0xD20 <
need=0x1370` on its face reads as H-ltexOOM-sel confirmed (selected pool
lacks a block big enough) — but the diagnostic's own reason field overrides
that with `corrupt`, because the raw pool walk hit `rsm_corrupt=1`
somewhere. Reading the raw per-pool dump (`fixup_game_funcs.py`'s
`rs-malloc-diag` block, `funcs_0.c`): pool 4 (unselected) and pool 0
(selected) both walk cleanly to their terminator; **pool E8 — the other
selected pool — stops with `stop=bad_size` at node index 55 of a walk that
had found 54 valid-looking nodes first** (`nnodes=56 nfree=1 maxfree=0x20`,
i.e. the only free block found before the break was tiny, 0x20 bytes).
Notably, an EARLIER `posctrl` sample from the same run (an unrelated
successful large allocation, printed first in the log since posctrl captures
the first 8 successes) shows pool E8 healthy at that earlier point in time:
`stop=term dumped=6 nnodes=6 nfree=2 maxfree=0x4E6290` (~5 MB free). So
whatever breaks the E8 walk develops **during the run**, between that
earlier successful allocation and the `ltexmg` attempt — not a permanently
malformed pool.

**This is genuinely new information, not previously seen:** neither the s627
global-OOM check (O1, REFUTED) nor the s627 size-corruption check (O3,
REFUTED) exercised the SELECTED pool's own walk integrity — those checked
"is there free space somewhere" and "is the requested size sane," not
"does the freelist chain in the pool `rs_malloc` actually searches stay
sane end to end." `reason=corrupt` had appeared once before (s627, folded
into the `no_fit_mystery` diag-artifact finding) but was never traced to a
specific pool/node before now.

### Instrument gap fixed same session
The raw node at the break point (i=55, pool E8) was read by the diagnostic
(`rsm_f`/`rsm_bsz` are computed unconditionally before the sanity check) but
never printed — the per-node `fprintf` was gated to free nodes or the first
8 allocated nodes per pool (log-budget rule), and node 55 was neither.
Fixed in `fixup_game_funcs.py` (N64Recomp sibling repo, `funcs_0.c`
rs-malloc-diag patch block): the print gate now also fires when the node
fails its own sanity check (`!rsm_sane`), so the NEXT occurrence of
`stop=bad_size` will show the actual raw `flags`/`size` at the break —
letting us tell real heap corruption (garbage bytes) apart from a walker
bug (a legitimate block shape the sanity check wrongly rejects, e.g. a
sentinel/terminator pattern this walk doesn't special-case). Full regen
pipeline run this session: `make_elf.py` → `N64Recomp` → `fixup_game_funcs.py`
→ `cmake --build`, all clean. `fixup_game_funcs.py` itself remains untracked
in the N64Recomp sibling repo (as it has been for the whole campaign — not
part of this repo's `lib/`, no `export.sh` applicable).

Combined across s628-s633 (13 attempts total): recovery fired 5/13 (was
4/11); of those, `thr11d_new` completed in 2/5 = 40% (was 1/4 = 25%) —
`H-thr11destroy-rate` stays SUPPORTED, sample still small (N=5).
`H-shipcycle2` (2nd ship-store/zero cycle correlates with `thr11d_new`
completing) is now 2/2: both `thr11d_new=1` samples (s629 att4, s633 att1)
had `ship_store=2 ship_zero_post=2`; every no-destroy attempt has had
`ship_store=1`. Still N=2 — promoted from "weak lead" to "supported, small
N," not yet a closeable claim.

|---|---|

Read `rs_malloc` freelist advance at `funcs_0.c:0x80001BEC–0x80001C00`:
`next = node + size + 0x10`, terminator flag bit 0x8 at next header — **exact match**
to the diagnostic's contiguous walk. Early posctrl E8 nodes also verify
`addr[i+1] = addr[i] + size[i] + 0x10` bit-exact. Therefore s633's
`stop=bad_size` at E8 i=55 is not a walker-model artifact. Predicted bad-node
address from i=54 free `@0x801F3C90 size=0x20`: **`0x801F3CC0`**. The break is

size field is truly insane the remaining free is unreachable to both game and
diag — explaining selected-pool null `rs_malloc(0x136C)` despite pool4 having
≥ need free (unselected). Still need the !sane print of raw flags/size at
`0x801F3CC0` on the next fail136c to distinguish size=0 / huge / pointer-shaped.

### Static freelist writer audit (item -391 / -385)

Node layout (rs_malloc walk L_80001BC4..): flags halfword @+0 (1=free, 2=alloc, 8=term),
size word @+4, next = addr + size + 0x10.

| Writer | flags/size stores | Can produce flags=0 size=0? |
|--------|-------------------|-----------------------------|
| rs_malloc alloc | flags=2; size=req (exact) or split | **No** — residual only if rem≥0x20; residual size = rem−0x10 ≥ 0x10 |
| rs_free | flags=1 only; size preserved; coalesce grows size | **No** — never zeros size |
| coalesceFreeHeapBlocks | flags=1; size merge | **No** |
| buildHeapFreeList / initMainHeap | flags=1; size=pool−0x20; term size=0 with flags&8 | **No** for !term zero-node |

**H-zero-free REFUTED (static).** **H-split-bug REFUTED (static).**
**H-never-init REFUTED** for mid-run i=55 after healthy posctrl (s638 dual-source dump).

### Discriminating dump (att2, same-run posctrl OK×8)

```
[cimg-raw] KILLER #1 task=0x768D40 byteOff=0xF8 w0=0xFFFFF488 w1=0x771F0D74
  w=1161 addr=0x1F0D74 wrap_n=5035810

  prev-1 op=0x00 w0=0x000D0000
[set-cimg-full #10706] KILLER addr=0x1F0D74 w=1161 siz=3 fmt=7 dl=0x768D40
[ost-wb] ALLOW_WILD_FL #1 ... HIT_WRITE_RESTORE
```

Att1: ok=8 wild=40 killer=0 (no exact). Att2: killer=1 fb_hit=1 in_wrap=41.

### ORIGIN (required before further freelist mitigation)

- **Immediate host writer of freelist stomp:** RT64 `copyNativeToRAM` color
  writeback of SETCIMG `addr=0x1F0D74` `w=1161` (range covers freelist phys
  `0x1F3CC0`). Product path ALLOW_WILD_FL + multi-header restore then repairs
  the 16B headers (match=1 same dump).
- **Why those operands exist:** length-respecting RDP walker over a
  **just-wrapped DPC ring** (`in_wrap=1`, ring start=`0x766000`) interprets
  garbage bytes as `G_SETCIMG` (op `0x3F`). Prev command ring is non-monotonic
  (zeros, nonsense `0x3F`), not a clean allowlist-width chain.
- **Legitimate?** **No.** This game never uses width 1161; same class as hangar
  wilds (s662: 104/104 `in_wrap=1` after garbage TRI). Hangar cluster uses ring
  start=`0x781800`; killer uses `0x766000` — shared class, different ring
  instance.
- **Not** a deferred-merge artifact outside submit: sticky
  `submit=[0x768D40,0x7699D0)` contains the killer task.

### Ruled out

- Exact killer as legitimate ucode emission (H-exact-legit).
- Exact killer as submit-range merge bug with empty sticky (H-exact-submit-range).
- Need for more freelist writeback mitigation layers before origin settled.

### Product implication

Freelist restore layers (s653–s660) are still correct as **defense** while
garbage CIMG still reaches writeback. Root fix is **stop feeding wrap-stale
ring content into processRDPLists** (or drop those submits), then A/B freelist
mitigation OFF expecting stomp rate → 0.

with freelist restore OFF. Expect: KILLER=0, freelist to_zero freelist-shaped=0,

## Session 664 — wrap-tail submit filter: Outcome B (false-drop; too coarse)

### Work unit

`src/rsp/dpc_bridge.cpp`: at live + deferred `submit_rdp_range` commit sites,
if `submit_lo ∈ [last_wrap_start, last_wrap_seen)` log `[dpc-wrap-drop]` and

`[dpc] DROP_WRAP_RDP=1 ...` on first enable.

A/B/C freeroll (same binary, sequential arms, force6/inject hangar path):
- **A:** filter ON + product restore ON
- **B:** filter ON + `ROGUESQ_FL_HDR_RESTORE=0`
- **C:** filter OFF + `ROGUESQ_FL_HDR_RESTORE=0` (control)

### Hypotheses

| ID | Claim | Result |
|----|-------|--------|
| H-wrap-filter-kills-killer | Filter zeroes KILLER + freelist stomp with restore OFF | **UNEVALUABLE** — filter never reached hangar/killer window |
| H-wrap-filter-false-drop | Filter drops legitimate post-wrap ring reuse (cinematic dies, hangar black) | **CONFIRMED dual-source (A+B)** |
| H-filter-needs-byte-granularity | Task-address in_wrap sticky is too coarse | **SUPPORTED** (same mechanism as false-drop) |

### Discriminating evidence

**A** (`s664_A_filter_restore_1_*`): banner=1; `[dpc-wrap-drop]` counter to
#29696 (rate-limited log lines 45); **all drops against single wrap start
`0x4B7800`** with seen growing to ~`0x4D3598`. OK×8 early boot LIVE
(tasks at `0x777880` outside that ring). **wild=0, vi1024=0, force6=0,
pngs=0**. SIGBUS mid-cinematic (`cinematicLoopBody` ←
`traverseSceneGraphRecursive` / `submitSceneNodeRender`). ~40s death.

**B** (`s664_B_filter_norestore_1_*`): identical shape to A (banner, ~30k
drops, OK×8, wild=0, cinematic SIGBUS). Restore OFF irrelevant — never
reached freelist stomp window.

**C** (`s664_C_nofilter_norestore_1_*`, posctrl control): drop=0; OK×8
wild=40 **killer=1** exact `task=0x768D40 w=1161 addr=0x1F0D74 in_wrap=1
submit=[0x768D40,0x7699D0)`; `ALLOW_WILD_FL` + `HIT_WRITE` (restore=0);
immediate freelist-shaped `to_zero prev_f=0x2 prev_sz=0x60` @ t=168799ms;
zero_node follow-on. Reconfirms s663 ORIGIN under restore OFF.

### Mechanism of false-drop

Sticky wrap `[start,seen)` never expires. After ring `0x4B7800` wraps once,
every subsequent **legitimate** rewrite of that ring has `submit_lo` still
inside sticky and is dropped forever (~30k drops). Hangar/killer rings
(`0x781800` / `0x766000`) never reached because cinematic already starved.

This is the same address space the game *reuses* after wrap — not a brief
"stale tail" window. Coarse task-lo ∈ sticky cannot distinguish garbage
decode from legitimate re-emit.

### ORIGIN (unchanged from s663)

```
ORIGIN: freelist stomp host writer = RT64 copyNativeToRAM color writeback of
SETCIMG addr=0x1F0D74 w=1161 (covers freelist phys 0x1F3CC0). Operands are
NOT legitimate — length-respecting RDP walk over just-wrapped DPC ring.
Filter at submit_lo∈sticky is too coarse; keep product freelist restore.
```

### Ruled out

- Productizing `ROGUESQ_DROP_WRAP_RDP` as default-ON task-address filter.
- Expecting freelist-restore retirement from this filter shape.

### Product

Keep `ROGUESQ_DROP_WRAP_RDP` default **OFF** (debug/experiment only).
Product freelist multi-header restore remains defense-in-depth.

### Next (-417)

Narrower root fix candidates (rank):
1. **Garbage-prev SETCIMG drop** inside processRDPLists / setColorImage:
   reject wild SETCIMG when prev ring is non-monotonic garbage (zeros /
   op 0x3F / non-allowlist) — targets decode site, not whole submit.
2. **Byte-offset desync**: only drop the *tail past last consumed high-water
   that was never rewritten* — requires tracking which ring bytes were
   re-written post-wrap (harder).
3. Keep freelist restore; treat wrap-stale as permanent class residual until
   (1) lands.

While hand-verifying the confirming run, noticed the existing
`[dl-sync-probe]` instrument (already firing every task under the freeroll's
standard `ROGUESQ_LOG_DL_SYNC=1`, no new instrumentation needed) had never
been tallied in aggregate before — only spot-read per-task. Scoped to
lines `>= sec2_ln=347715` (post-sec2 mission phase only) in the same
`pulse_2_20260811200701/run.log`:

- 29780 `[dl-sync-probe]` lines post-sec2. `e9_a`/`e9_b` (proper
  control-flow-respecting tree walks, one treating opcode 0xB5 as
  end-of-DL, one not) are BOTH zero in 18452/29780 (~62%), but **11328/29780
  (~38%) show e9_a>0 or e9_b>0** — i.e. a large fraction of post-sec2
  mission tasks DO contain the SYNC_FULL byte value in their raw command
  walk.
- Cross-referenced against the same window's `[runner] task ... syncs=`
  field (the runner's own translated/dispatched RDP command count, the
  actual signal `rdpFs`/item -421's plateau is measured from): **29777/29780
  post-sec2 tasks report `syncs=0`; only 3 show `syncs=1`.**

Read together: a large fraction of post-sec2 mission DLs contain what the
naive fixed-8-byte-stride walker sees as an E9 opcode, yet the runner's own
translated-command counter almost never registers a real sync. Two
competing explanations, NOT yet distinguished:
- **H-e9-not-translated:** the guest DL genuinely contains SYNC_FULL
  requests that our RDP command translator/dispatcher drops or fails to
  execute for this task class — would directly explain the -421 plateau as
  a translation-path bug, not a content-absence issue.
- **H-e9-walker-misaligned:** `walk_tree`'s fixed 8-byte stride (used for
  `e9_a`/`e9_b`) does not account for the F5 ucode's variable-length
  inline-data commands (MoveMem/TriGen/Tri/TexrectGen/SetOtherMode_*_EX —
  see `docs/F5-UCODE-REFERENCE.md`), unlike the existing
  `ROGUESQ_LOG_DL_SYNC2` six-command-aware walker (built for the
  cimg-origin-desync investigation, `-415..-417`). An unaligned walk can
  land mid-command and read a coincidental 0xE9 byte that isn't a real
  opcode boundary — the 38% hit rate could be entirely this artifact.

Not adjudicated this session (out of scope for the assigned -422 work
unit; flagging per iron rule 5 "check the boring thing first" — an
instrumentation alignment bug is the boring explanation and must be ruled
out before H-e9-not-translated enters CURRENT-TRUTH). Full next-step design
in `scratch/agent/NEXT.md`.

- H-menu-return-input CONFIRMED (was SUPPORTED single-source in s670).
- Old `wrapper.stdout` leftover data reconfirmed as already-closed s670

## Session 674 (2026-08-12) — HARNESS: codex runner made viable; two loop bugs fixed

Not an experiment iteration. Toolchain work on `tools/agent/`, prompted by the
first `RUNNER=codex` runs (s673 and the 00:21 restart).

**s673's "no SDL display" was the codex SANDBOX, not the terminal context.**
`codex exec` defaulted to `-s workspace-write`, which is a seatbelt sandbox.
Measured directly in a throwaway `/tmp` git repo (codex-cli 0.144.3), inside
that sandbox vs an ordinary shell:

| probe | `-s workspace-write` | unsandboxed / `danger-full-access` |
|---|---|---|
| `test -w .git` | `GIT_READONLY` | `GIT_WRITABLE` |
| `nice -n 5 true` | `setpriority: Operation not permitted` | `nice_rc=0` |
| `launchctl managername` | `Aqua` | `Aqua` |

So the session type was never the problem — the seatbelt was. Three
consequences, the middle one previously misdiagnosed:

1. The game gets no display ("The video driver did not add any displays",
   `hsel=0`, clean exit in 3-4s) because the work is GUI-driven and that is
   exactly what the sandbox blocks. Still to be confirmed at full access.
2. **CORRECTION to s673's checkpoint.** It concluded the read-only `.git` was
   "specific to that one sandbox invocation, not a durable property". It is
   deterministic: EVERY codex iteration under workspace-write gets a read-only
   `.git`, so no codex iteration can ever meet an exit contract that ends in a
   commit. s673's commit landed because `loop.sh` routes contract RETRIES to
   the claude runner, which is unsandboxed — the retry, not a changed sandbox,
   is what "found `.git` writable". Attribution error of the familiar kind: two
   observations from two different processes read as one process changing.
3. `nice(5) denied`, which s673 reported without attribution, is the same cause.

Fix: `runner.sh` codex sandbox default raised to `danger-full-access`, with the
measurements inline so it is not quietly lowered again. `RUNNER_SANDBOX` still
overrides per run.

**Loop bug: a run could die on a BLOCKED.md that says it is not blocked.**
`loop.sh` halted on the mere EXISTENCE of `scratch/agent/BLOCKED.md`. s673 ended
`STATUS=DONE` / `OUTCOME=ADVANCED` but left behind a BLOCKED.md whose first line
read `# Not currently blocked`, so the 00:21 codex run exited before preflight,
before spending anything, on a healthy repo. Fixed on both sides: an iteration
ending DONE has its leftover BLOCKED.md archived, and the loop top only treats
the file as stale when STATUS=DONE *and* its first line says "not blocked" — a
real block (STATUS=BLOCKED) and a preflight block ("# Blocked by preflight")
are both still honoured.

**Known blind spot, not yet fixed:** `preflight.sh` runs in loop.sh's own shell
and then hands the work to a runner that may be sandboxed, so for codex it
certifies an environment the agent never gets. It printed `[preflight] OK` at
00:05:16 immediately before an agent that could not open a window. Its very
first check (`launchctl managername` = Aqua) passes inside the sandbox too, so
it cannot catch this class by itself — the fix is to run it inside the runner.

### Rules out / confirms
- Confirms the codex workspace-write sandbox blocks `.git` writes and
  `setpriority`, deterministically, in a repo unrelated to this one.
- Refutes s673's "one-off sandbox invocation" reading of the read-only `.git`.
- Does NOT yet confirm the game gets a display under `danger-full-access`; the
  00:21 run that would have shown it never started. Refutation test:
  `RUNNER=codex ITER_CAP=1 caffeinate -dis tools/agent/loop.sh` from a GUI
  session, then check whether the SDL display error recurs.

### Residual → item -421 unchanged; the E9-alignment discriminator still needs one GUI-session run.

## Session 676 (2026-08-12) — item -421: E9 loss is before authoritative RDP dispatch

Built the three-stage discriminator under `ROGUESQ_LOG_E9_DISPATCH=1` and ran
`env BUDGET_S=2400 zsh scratch/agent/s670_postsec2_pulse_freeroll.sh`.
The first build instrumented `processDisplayLists`; the live LLE-solo path is
`processRDPLists`, so pre/handler positive controls were zero and that run was
discarded. The corrected build instrumented raw opcode decode in
`processRDPLists`, `GBI_RDP::fullSync`, and `State::fullSync`.

Positive control passed in the same run: millions of authoritative commands,
nonzero E7 and E9, and matching display-list counters across
`stage=pre` → `stage=handler` → `stage=state`. Attempt 5 was recovery-active,
reached section 2, fired the established input pulse, and held thr13 alive.
After the section-2 marker, `[dl-sync-probe2]` reported 13,132 task probes,
6,719 with `e9_aligned>0`, aligned E9 sum 32,150. Across the same window the
authoritative parser's cumulative E9 counter advanced by only 2 (E7 delta 0);
all authoritative E9s that appeared reached the handler and State stages.

This confirms H-e9-pre-dispatch-loss. It rules out map/handler replacement and
State/runner accounting as the dominant loss: those stages preserve every E9

## Session 818 (2026-08-13) — static VI frame field is ROM-initialized

The bounded source/data audit traced the static frame object used by both

(`rom=0x1040`, `vram=0x80000440`). The retail ROM bytes at that offset are:
`00 00 00 00 80 03 DF A0 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 01 40 00 E0 00 10`.
Thus `D_80037574` (`D_80037560+0x14`) is the initialized big-endian halfword
`0x00E0`; the record's `+0x04` word is the `mainGameLoop` pointer
`0x8003DFA0`.

`0x8006B3E0` directly loads `lhu 0x7574($v0)`, while the absolute-address
search found no generated store targeting `0x80037574`. The static field is
therefore **H-static-field-rom-intended**, not a hidden runtime-writer case.
This resolves the initializer question but does not assign the field's full
semantic role or explain the later VI phase. No build, run, code change, or
mitigation was made.

ORIGIN: the value originates in the retail ROM initializer at VROM `0x38174`;
it is a legitimate static data value, not a corruption mitigation target.

## Session 835 (2026-08-13) — source audit identifies command-boundary E9 overcount

Performed the prescribed bounded parser-side source audit; no build, run, or
runtime behavior changed. `MEM_B` uses the host index `logical_address ^ 3`,
so the bridge's `g_rdram_for_submit[p ^ 3]` test and RT64's
`DisplayList::w0 >> 24` load select the same logical first byte. H-byte-order
is refuted.

The bridge counter scans every 8-byte slot from `lo` through `hi`, whereas the
RT64 direct parser advances by `cmdLength * sizeof(DisplayList)`. Therefore an
E9 at an interior word of a multiword command is counted by the bridge but is
not a parser command fetch. Pending completion has a separate gate requiring
completed bytes, raw pending opcode E9, the authoritative callback, and a
non-sentinel `s_rs64_pending_start_address`; that sentinel is set only when a
raw E9 command crosses a range boundary. This explains a lower parser count
without byte-order loss, while leaving pending-only effects to a paired probe.

This source result is single-source evidence. It identifies command-boundary
filtering as the leading explanation for s833's late rows (570=9/1, 580=9/1,
632=27/0, 649=31/3), but does not promote it to settled truth until a
phase-gated probe records bridge slots and parser command starts by address.
No mitigation or legitimacy claim was made.

ORIGIN: no game value, RDP command, mitigation, or runtime behavior changed;
this iteration changed only audit prose and scratch control files.

## Session 839 (2026-08-13) — source audit finds synthetic stale-label path

Performed the prescribed source-only audit of the submit-to-parser chain; no
build or run was performed. Normal accepted bridge ranges call
`rs64_dpc_record_submit`, store their range, increment the submit serial, and
immediately call `submit_rdp_range`. That call synchronously invokes RT64 with
the same `[lo,hi)` arguments, and `processRDPLists` derives its parser range
from the same pointers. This rules out a normal producer/consumer range race
and normal latest-submit ordering as explanations for s838's ordinary rows.

The audit found one bounded exception: non-deferred synthetic FULL_SYNC
injection in `rsp_force_fullsync` calls `submit_rdp_range(addr, addr + 8)`

## Session 852 (2026-08-13) — source audit accounts for span matches; residual remains outside normal condition paths

Performed the prescribed bounded source-only audit; no build or run was
performed. The bridge's accepted ordinary ranges are scanned in 8-byte steps
and read the logical first byte through the same byte-swapped RDRAM mapping
used to reconstruct words. Each accepted range is recorded, serialised, and
passed synchronously to `submit_rdp_range`; RT64 derives its parser call range
from the same `[lo, hi)` pointers.

The authoritative parser loads the command opcode at each current boundary,
uses `commandWordLengths[opCode]`, reports a `direct` condition only when the
raw opcode is E9, reports a `span` condition for every normal non-E9 command,
and advances by `cmdLength * 8`. Thus an E9 byte at an interior 8-byte slot is
intentionally bridge-counted but is inline data in the preceding parser
command. The pending path records a split command only when a command crosses
the current `[lo, hi)` end and reports it on completion; the captured zero
pending rows are consistent with that gate. Deferred ranges receive normal
submit identity at commit. The non-deferred synthetic FULL_SYNC path is the
only submit path that bypasses `rs64_dpc_record_submit` and can carry a stale
serial/range label, but it submits only `[addr, addr+8)`.

This source table selects H-span-intended for the 1,001 span rows and rules out
a normal byte-order or producer/consumer range mismatch. It does not classify
the one residual condition-join slot: the normal direct/span paths are
complete, while the extended-opcode branch bypasses both condition callbacks
and uses its own function-controlled advancement. The residual therefore
needs one behavior-neutral runtime marker at that branch before choosing
between H-extended-residual and the bounded synthetic-label edge. No writer,
operand-legitimacy, parser-behavior, or mitigation conclusion follows.

ORIGIN: source audit only; no game value, RDP command, parser advancement, or
mitigation behavior changed.
